**Total Test Cases:** 37,901 — the sum of `scripts/test-case-floors.json`,
which is the per-invocation `pass + skipped` measured on a CLEAN

This number is CHECKED now, per workspace rather than in aggregate — see the

TWO EARLIER RUNS OF THE SAME TREE EACH FAILED ON A DIFFERENT FILE, both
`testTimeoutFailure` at exactly 30,000 ms, and neither was a logic error — the
suite runs `--test-concurrency=4` against a 30 s PER-FILE wall, so a file whose
isolated cost is a large fraction of that tips over under load. One was fixed
(`mf-portfolio-as-on` re-read a 2.6 MB / 121-sheet fixture nine times: 9.3 s ->
3.9 s); the other, `apps/web/__tests__/research/fetch-short-interest.test.ts`,
is 14.8 s in isolation and unrelated to that branch. **Read the turbo task
accounting, not the exit code** — the first of those runs exited 0.

**THAT WALL IS A PER-FILE BUDGET, AND IT COVERS MODULE LOAD** (MONEY-1489).
`--test-timeout` is documented per-TEST and node treats each FILE as a test, so
the budget spans the whole child process — measured, not inferred: a file that
burns 5 s at MODULE SCOPE is cancelled by `--test-timeout=3000` exactly like one
that burns it inside `it()`. So "hoist the expensive `require()` out of the
measured suite" moves nothing; only making it CHEAPER does. Both files killed
in CI #713/#727/#729 paid a cold `require("@usemoney/services")` — **3817 ms**,
because that barrel re-exports ~40 services and drags in the research, roast and
PDF-renderer packages — where the SUBPATH actually needed costs **48 ms**.
`apps/web/__tests__/actions/coupon.test.ts` went **3243 ms -> 238 ms** on that
one line. The standing "import subpaths, never root barrels" rule is a
test-budget rule too.

`broker-sync-action-e2e.test.ts` is NOT fixed the same way, and the attempt was
REVERTED — worth writing down, because it looks like the obvious next step. Its
expensive `require` is the module UNDER TEST
(`apps/web/lib/actions/broker-connection.ts`), so narrowing it means
de-barrelling PRODUCTION code. Measured, that bought 3420 ms -> 3165 ms (**8%**)
— the test already stubs `@usemoney/core` and `@usemoney/email` out of the
graph, so the barrel was never the dominant cost inside it — and it broke **9
tests** across the broker suites: they seam the services layer by purging
`packages/services/src/index.` from `require.cache`, and a subpath import never
passes through `index.ts`, so the recorder saw zero calls. 8% is not worth
moving a production import and nine seams; that de-barrelling is its own ticket.

**THE WORST FILE IN THE REPO IS NEITHER OF THOSE.** Measured in isolation on a
14-core machine: `packages/core/__tests__/market-data/mf-portfolio-as-on.test.ts`
is **17.4 s — 58% of the 30 s budget**, so a 1.7x slowdown kills it;
`mf-portfolio-logic.test.ts` is 7.3 s (24%) and `commodity-eod-logic.test.ts`
3.6 s (12%). All three were observed CANCELLED in a parallel local
`yarn verify:push` on 2026-09-21. Note as-on had ALREADY had an optimisation
pass — the 9.3 s -> 3.9 s quoted above — and has grown back; 8.8 s of it is now
a SINGLE test that parses all four real AMC workbooks (5.9 MB), which is
inherent work rather than a repeated parse, so there is no cheap win left in it.

**AND THE COUNT IS CHECKED NOW.** This line used to read "NOT what
`test:coverage-check` validates — that gate reads only the FILE-COUNT headline,
so a per-file case count can rot without failing anything", which was true and
is the gap MONEY-1093 fell through (45 files / 3,093 cases silently never
executed, exit 0, every counter green, this document still counting them).
`scripts/test-timeout.ts` now compares each workspace invocation's EXECUTED case
count against a floor in `scripts/test-case-floors.json` and refuses a run that
drops below it. It complements rather than replaces `test:coverage-check`: that
gate reads the on-disk FILE inventory, this one reads what actually RAN.

> **62 of these files were not being EXECUTED until MONEY-1093.** The test glob
> `--test __tests__/**/*.test.ts` was unquoted, so the shell expanded `**` as a
> single `*`. It failed asymmetrically: where the shell glob matched nothing
> (`packages/research`, `packages/services` — files sit directly in `__tests__/`)
> the literal pattern reached node, whose glob IS recursive, and everything ran.
> Where it matched something (`apps/web`) the shell won and truncated the set —
> 45 files / 3,093 cases never ran, including every broker-adapter test and both
> sector-taxonomy files, while this document counted them. The pattern only
> worked in the workspaces where it failed. Per workspace: apps/web 45,
> packages/core 14, apps/admin 1, apps/api 1, workers 1 = **62**.
>
> An earlier revision of this note said **154**, which was wrong and wrong in a
> revealing way: 154 is the number of files the SHELL glob missed, but in 11 of
> 16 workspaces the shell matched nothing so node ran everything anyway
> (62 + 92 = 154). The paragraph explained that asymmetry correctly and then
> stated the inflated figure as its headline — in the one commit whose entire
> thesis is that a counted-but-unexecuted number is dangerous.
>
> The glob is now quoted in all 16 workspace `package.json` files, which hands
> expansion to node everywhere. Every previously-hidden file passed except one
> deliberate taxonomy guard.

> **Run the suite serialized.** `yarn test` (turbo default concurrency) spawns
> all ~10 workspace `node:test` processes at once; on a loaded machine some get
> killed (force-exit / timeout), which turbo reports as a failed TASK even though
> zero test CASES failed. Verify with `turbo run test --concurrency=1` (optionally
> `--force` to bypass cache) — that is the authoritative green check.

> **MONEY-1085 — the bhavcopy NSE drop + raw-feed archive (2026-07-28):** the
> daily ingest fetched ~3,181 NSE rows and resolved only ~2,415, silently
> dropping ~766 closing prices EVERY trading day on BOTH envs. Verified against
> live prod: the 766 are exactly SM 324 / BE 278 / ST 125 / BZ 39, splitting 448
> absent from `instrument_mappings`, 256 present as NSE rows but
> `isActive:false`, 293 present only as their BSE row. Root cause was the
> instrument UNIVERSE, not the price feed — the Zerodha Kite dump omits NSE's
> SME/book-entry series and has no ISIN column at all (`isin` was empty on all
> 25,473 rows). Fix: `NseMasterInstrumentProvider` over NSE's two public master
> CSVs (2,387 main-board + 558 SME = 2,945 unique symbols, all with ISINs).
>
> Note the fix is NOT "populate isin": `buildInstrumentIndex` keyed `byIsin`
> exchange-agnostically and first-wins, so populating it alone would have
> resolved those 293 rows to their BSE instrument and written NSE closes onto
> BSE instruments (`DailyPrice` is keyed `[instrumentId, date]` with no exchange
> column). The key is now `ISIN@EXCHANGE` and the pre-existing test that
> asserted the cross-exchange resolve as intended behaviour is inverted.
>
> Also adds a GCS raw-feed archive (`market-data/feed-archive.ts`,
> `FEED_ARCHIVE_MODE=archive|replay`, unset = passthrough) so prod fetches each
> exchange file once and QA replays the same bytes through its OWN ingest —
> chosen over a Mongo mirror because `daily_prices`/`latest_quotes`/
> `intraday_bars`/`stock_profiles` key on `instrumentId`, a foreign ObjectId QA
> generates itself. New tests: `nse-master-logic` (20), `feed-archive` (19),
> `no-feed-fetch-bypass` (3); `bhavcopy-sync-logic` 18→19. +3 files / +42 cases.
> All eight new guards mutation-tested (break the source, confirm red) —
> including reverting the ISIN key to the original bug, which turns 3 tests red.
>

> **Follow-up — the NSE JSON seam, per function (MONEY-1189 audit gap #6,
> 2026-08-13).** `fetchNSEAnnouncements`, `fetchNSEFinancialResults` and
> `fetchNSECorporateActions` fetched NSE and threw the raw bytes away while
> three siblings in the SAME file archived correctly — so the announcements
> feed (annual reports, categorized filings, the `annual-reports-sync` worker)
> never reached `archiveNseJsonResponse` at all. Both scans above were blind to
> it twice over: they only walk `packages/core/src`, and FILE granularity
> cannot see a bypass in a file that already archives from three other
> functions. `no-feed-fetch-bypass` 10→17 adds a per-FUNCTION scan over
> `packages/research/src` — a block that talks HTTP to NSE must hand its raw
> response to the seam; cookie handshakes and attachment (PDF) downloads are
> excluded structurally, and the three remaining non-archiving readers
> (`nse-client`/`nse-fii-dii` `nseFetch`, `screener-client`) are exemptions with
> written reasons, two of them recorded as OPEN gaps rather than absolutions.
> New: `nse-filings-archive` (11) — functional, `globalThis.fetch` stubbed,
> pinning that each fetcher consults the seam with the SAME path it fetched,
> that a body the domain parser rejects is archived anyway, and (on the
> market-wide bulk leg, the one that actually writes) that the stored bytes are
> byte-for-byte what NSE served and a rejected write leaves the rows intact.
> **+1 file / +18 cases.** Verified red-before/green-after by running both
> suites against the pre-fix source: 3 named offenders in the scan, 4 failures
> in the functional file.
>
> Note what the fix does NOT do: nothing new is WRITTEN to GCS. All three paths
> carry `symbol=`, which is `nseJsonArchiveKey`'s deliberate volume exclusion,
> so the seam declines them and counts a `skipped`. That is the point — "we
> asked and the policy said no" is a different state from "nobody asked", and
> only the first follows the policy if it ever changes.

> **Follow-up — MONEY-1158, the runtime half of item 6 (2026-08-10).** New:
> `brokers/token-exchange` (20). **+1 file / +20 cases.**
>
> The type fix shipped with MONEY-1157 made `access_token` non-optional in four
> broker clients, which only restated an assumption the code already made
> unconditionally — it added no runtime check. On a 200 whose body carried an
> error envelope instead of a token (a normal OAuth failure mode under rate
> limiting or a revoked app), `upstox`, `fyers` and `interactive-brokers`
> returned `accessToken: undefined` and `zerodha` threw a bare TypeError. The
> caller encrypts and persists that value, so the connection LOOKS established
> while every later sync fails against a credential that was never real.
>
> The tests drive the REAL `static exchangeToken()` of each client against a
> stubbed `fetch`, from ONE table — so a new broker client cannot quietly skip
> the guard without being added to it. Three assertions per client: a 200 error
> envelope throws (never returns undefined), the throw is classified `payload`
> rather than `transport` (which is what makes a `BrokerIntegrationFailure` row
> triageable without re-reading the message), and the happy path still returns a
> token — the last of these stopping the guard from "passing" by rejecting
> everything. `requireAccessToken` also rejects the empty string, which is
> encryptable and persistable in exactly the same way as `undefined`.
>
> Mutation-verified: reverting Zerodha's guard alone fails precisely its own
> case (18/19 pass), so the suite is bound to the shipped guards.
>
> One case exists because the first attempt at this fix broke something. The
> shared helper originally COMPOSED a tidy message
> (`"<Broker> token exchange failed: HTTP <n> — <upstream>"`), which the
> pre-existing `zerodha-token-exchange-contract` test caught: broker error
> messages here are load-bearing strings. `mapKnownBrokerError` matches
> `"zerodha: the user is not enabled"` to render a specific support card, and
> `classifyBrokerError` derives `errorClass`/`recoveryAction` by substring — so
> the tidy wrapper lost the card AND, because it contains the word "token",
> would have reclassified every 5xx as AUTH_EXPIRED with a "reauth" recovery
> action. The helper now takes the message as a parameter and each client keeps
> its exact historical string; the classification lives only in the typed
> fields. `does NOT rewrite the message it is given` pins that.
>
> `hdfc.ts` and `icici.ts` already guarded correctly and were deliberately left
> alone — their messages are load-bearing in existing logs, and rewriting a
> working guard on a live credential path buys nothing.
>

> fetched ~161 NSE index closes every trading day and discarded them ("no
> index-history model yet"), so there was no index history to benchmark a
> portfolio against — and NSE only serves a limited window, so each day
> discarded was unrecoverable. New `IndexClose` model keyed on a normalised
> slug rather than NSE's display name, which is cosmetically unstable
> ("Nifty 50" vs "NIFTY 50") and would fork one index's history into two.
> `bhavcopy-sync-logic` 25→30; mutation-tested (dropping the case fold turns
> 3 red).

> **MONEY-853 — scraper 429 hardening (2026-06-19):** the whole-market weekly
> scrape exhausted Screener's per-IP quota → a sustained 429 wall → ZERO screener
> data ever reached GCS (only Tickertape `financial_statement` landed; diagnosed
> from QA worker logs + the empty `stocks/{SYM}/screener_*` GCS prefixes). Fixed
> with ONE reusable trio applied to BOTH scrapers: (1) client-side retry with
> exponential backoff honouring `Retry-After`; (2) a typed
> `ScreenerRateLimitError` / `BseRateLimitError` that PROPAGATES so the worker can
> (3) circuit-break the run instead of tar-pitting a rate-limited host. Plus
> per-run caps (`API_LIMITS.screener` 2000→500; new `MAX_PDF_DOWNLOADS_PER_RUN`
> for the BSE attachment host). Wired into all THREE consumers:
> `stock-document-sync`, `bse-announcements-sync`, and `corporate-actions-sync`
> (which previously SWALLOWED the typed 429 per-symbol and would have tar-pitted
> the whole held universe). BSE backoff is env-tunable + read per-call so tests
> shrink it. Tests: `bse-client` +5 (shape + 429 retry/propagation/degrade);
> `processor-stock-document-sync` cap assertion 2000→500. Needs worker redeploy.
> Pairs with the new **scrape-once-in-prod** model — `setup-scheduler.sh` now
> makes every external-data cron PROD-ONLY and `scripts/ops/sync-prod-to-qa.sh`
> copies the reference data + GCS down to QA, so QA never hits a third-party host.
> Build 21/21, test 24/24 (15,657 web `# pass`, 0 fail).

> FNV-1a hash; set on connect + backfilled via
> `scripts/ops/backfill-syncbucket.ts`), each synced in parallel. + per-user
> idempotency guard (skip if an in-flight BROKER_SYNC job exists), dead-letter
> policy on all worker push subs, and sharded crons now re-pair each bucket user
> whose trades changed (`needsRepairing`). Tests:
> `syncBucketFor`/fan-out/idempotency/bucket-where-clause + the bucket-pairing
> case. ~+30 cases.

> ### ⚠️ Two different "coverage" numbers — do not conflate them
>
> This report's headline figures (the `~94%` in [Overall Coverage
> Summary](#overall-coverage-summary)) measure **by-name file coverage** — i.e.
> _"does this source file have at least one test that exercises it?"_. That is a
> breadth metric, NOT executed line coverage.
>
> **Executed line coverage (c8, V8) is ~14% today.** The two diverge because a
> file can be "tested" (has a test that imports it) while the test only drives a
> few of its branches. The de-couple / negative-edge program on this epic
> (MONEY-620, e.g. the shadow-test removal + security regression suites below)
> is what raises the _executed_ number over time.
>
> The live executed number is emitted by `yarn test:coverage` (c8
> `text-summary`, non-blocking). There is deliberately **no enforced coverage
> floor** yet — see the TODO in `.github/workflows/test.yml` to ratchet one once
> the executed number climbs. **Aspirational target:** ≥90% executed lines on
> `apps/web` + every `packages/*` with tests (NOT yet met — by-name breadth is
> already ~94%, executed lines are ~14%).

### Test tiers (MONEY-620)

The suite runs in three tiers (full detail in
[`scripts/README.md` → "Test tiers"](./scripts/README.md)):

| Tier           | Command           | Scope                                                                                                                                                                                             | Env                           |
| -------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| **smoke**      | `yarn test:smoke` | Critical-path subset (`scripts/smoke-list.txt`): FIFO pairing, calc-suite, guardrails, webhook sig/idempotency + `*-e2e`, demo routes, `security/*`, subscription, contract tests. Runs in < 60s. | None (pure/mocked)            |
| **regression** | `yarn test`       | The WHOLE suite (`turbo run test`). CI merge gate.                                                                                                                                                | None (mocked)                 |
| **full**       | `yarn test:full`  | Regression **+** env-gated `tests/integration/**` (`RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=true`).                                                                                                                 | QA DB + Redis for integration |

**Shadow-test removal campaign (2026-06-05, branch `fix/MONEY-619`):** Swept the
suite for "shadow" tests — ones that reimplemented source logic inline and
asserted the copy (green even while the real code breaks). **~53 shadow test
files de-shadowed** to exercise the REAL exported source: 32 fully-inline (first
inventory) + 3 residual MIXED (Zerodha checksum, Gemini guardrails ×2, found via
T117/T119) + 18 MIXED in admin/content/services (second-pass scan); plus 3 stale
red assertions corrected (Upstox MF support, Groww token validity). The pure
logic each test needed was extracted into exported, source-wired modules so the
production path and the test execute the SAME code — `lib/brokers/oauth-url.ts` +
`oauth-callback.ts` (7 callback routes), `lib/payments/plan-config.ts` +
clerk/dodo `*-webhook-logic.ts` (real `svix` verify + tamper-rejection contract
tests + MONEY-594 idempotency), `ZerodhaClient.generateChecksum`,
`lib/db/{dashboard,positions,trades}-logic.ts`, market `*-logic` +
`app/api/*/route-logic.ts`, `packages/core/src/gemini/guardrails-core.ts`, and
admin/content action `*-logic.ts` (WRITER-scoping / IDOR / requireAdmin guards
preserved byte-for-byte). Several shadows were caught asserting WRONG values
(stale demo data, drifted plan prices, a bogus ProPlanMode enum). Standing
policy: the new `.claude/skills/writing-tests` skill — never shadow, always
exercise the real exported symbol. Non-Zerodha broker client checksum de-shadows
are intentionally deferred (only Zerodha is wired in production).

**MONEY-883 Clerk `user.created` write-conflict retry (2026-06-29, branch `fix/MONEY-882`):** `ensureUserAndSubscription` 500'd (`prisma.user.create() … Transaction failed`, Prisma **P2034**) when the Clerk webhook raced the lazy `getOrCreateUser()` — both insert the same new row → MongoDB write conflict → new users never created. Added a bounded retry on transient conflicts. **+6 cases** in `apps/web/__tests__/services/user-sync-logic.test.ts` (now **14**) covering `isRetryableSyncError`: P2034 + P2002 by code, P2034 message text, bare `WriteConflict` / `deadlock`, non-retryable (P2025 / validation) rejected, null / non-Error rejected.

**MONEY-594 / MONEY-595 security regression suite (2026-06-01, branch
`fix/MONEY-594`):** Regression coverage for the security fixes on the branch.
**+82 cases** across 5 new files + 2 extended files (pure/mocked per repo
convention, no prisma/network):
`ssrf-guard.test.ts` (**45** — now imports and asserts the **REAL shipped
classifier** from `@usemoney/core/import` (`isBlockedIp` + the
`@internal`-exported `isBlockedIpv4` / `isBlockedIpv6` / `expandIpv6` /
`groupsToIpv4`) and the real `isSafeFetchTarget` — the inline mirror copies were
deleted, so a source regression now fails these tests. `isBlockedIp` blocks
169.254.169.254 / 10.x / 127.x / 172.16-31.x / 192.168.x / IPv6
loopback+ULA+link-local+v4-mapped metadata and ALLOWS public IPs; **IPv6
classifier-gap coverage (SCAN-FIND 5): HEX IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:7f00:1`),
IPv4-compatible (`::7f00:1` / `::127.0.0.1`), NAT64 (`64:ff9b::/96`), 6to4
(`2002::/16`) all blocked when the embedded v4 is private/metadata, site-local
`fec0::/10` blocked, and public IPv4 embedded in those v6 forms +
global-unicast `2000::/3` are NOT over-blocked**; **newly-blocked reserved IPv6
ranges (MONEY-594 residual): `fe00::/9` (fe00..fe7f) and `f800::/6`
(f800..fbff) fail closed, with the 2000::/3 global-unicast boundaries
(`2000::1` / `3fff:ffff::1`) asserted still-allowed**; direct
`expandIpv6` (zero-compression, dotted-quad-tail rewrite, invalid→null) +
`groupsToIpv4` + family-specific `isBlockedIpv4`/`isBlockedIpv6` coverage;
`classifyTarget` (a thin adapter over the real `isSafeFetchTarget`) blocks
metadata.google.internal / `metadata` / localhost hostnames, http/file/gopher
schemes, URL credentials, allowlist misses, the metadata IP reached via DNS,
and **bracketed IPv6 literal hosts
(`[::1]` / `[::ffff:169.254.169.254]` / `[64:ff9b::7f00:1]` / `[2002:7f00:1::]`)
classified as IP literals and rejected, while a bracketed public literal
`[2001:4860:4860::8888]` is allowed**; `guardedFetch` drives the real per-hop
`isSafeFetchTarget` and rejects a 302/301 → private-IP and over-limit redirect
loops; **plus a real two-lookup DNS-rebinding regression that drives the ACTUAL
exported `safeFetch`: a validator that resolves to a public IP while a trapped
connect-time `node:dns.lookup` would rebind to a loopback sentinel — asserting
safeFetch pins to the validated IP, never performs a second resolution, never
reaches the rebind sentinel, and still refuses a private-only resolution**);
`watchlist-reorder-idor.test.ts` (**5** — scoped `updateMany` leaves a victim's
smuggled item ids untouched (touched=0), surfaces a count-mismatch when foreign
ids are mixed in, and a pre-fix id-only write regression-asserts the
vulnerability the `watchlistId` scope closes);
`credit-atomic-decrement.test.ts` (**6** — at balance == cost-1 the conditional
`updateMany` matches zero rows / fails closed, the atomic `increment` makes two
interleaved charges debit twice (no double-spend), and the bounded retry fails

`demo-mode-resolver.test.ts` (**7** — resolver ignores a forged
`x-demo-mode: true` header, honors only a valid `sb_demo` cookie, and Clerk
session wins over a stale cookie);
`cron-auth.test.ts` (**+4**, now 11 — adds the MONEY-595
`apply-scheduled-plan-changes` route status-mapping contract: 503 unset / 401
missing+wrong / 200 exact, atop the existing MONEY-592 constant-time cases);
`__tests__/api/payments-callback.test.ts` (**+11**, now 36 — SCAN-FIND #67
payment-callback replay idempotency: models the `payment.updateMany({ where: {
id, appliedAt: null } })` claim and asserts the first claim grants (count===1),
replays lose the race, exactly one caller wins across 25 concurrent replays,
appliedAt is never overwritten, credit-pack credits do NOT stack across replays
(1000 once, not 3000), main-plan `creditsUsed` is NOT reset by a replay, and a
rejected payment never burns the claim because the claim runs only after the
validation guards pass; **plus SCAN-FIND #76 read-before-claim window**: the
FIXED claim-then-read path grants the pack exactly once under a concurrent race,

from the paid Payment record into `subscription.addons` while ignoring the

`security/paper-delete-idor.test.ts` (removed MONEY-1062 — the 4 IDOR cases now ride in the paper service suites; SCAN-FIND #76/#71 A01 IDOR:
`deletePaperTrade` scoped to `deleteMany({ where: { id, userId } })` deletes the
caller's own position, rejects a cross-user delete with not-found (victim row

**MONEY-1240 (2026-08-21, branch `fix/MONEY-1240`):** Ask FIRE answers stopped
mid-sentence, always exactly where a computed figure belonged ("…you would
achieve it" with no age). **Modified** `fire-chat-action.test.ts` (23 → **28**,
no new file). Two stacked defects: `maxOutputTokens` was 1024, which a
projection answer overruns, and `finishReason` was **never read anywhere**, so a
candidate that stopped on `MAX_TOKENS` was indistinguishable from one that
finished and the fragment rendered as a confident, complete reply. Reading
`finishReason` is the load-bearing half — without it, raising the cap only moves
the cliff. The stub now carries a `finishReason` (defaulting to `"STOP"`, so
every pre-existing case keeps its meaning). Cases: `[regression]` MAX*TOKENS on
a text-only turn returns an error rather than the fragment; `[regression]` a
truncated turn is NOT charged (the guard returns before `consumeCredits`);
MAX_TOKENS \_alongside* tool calls still returns, because the client executes
the call and hops again so the prose is not the final word — failing there would
strand an applied tool call; a normal `STOP` is unaffected; and the configured
budget must exceed the 1024 that truncated in production. Mutation-verified
independently: dropping the `finishReason` check fails 2, reverting the cap to
1024 fails 1.

**MONEY-1243 (2026-08-21, branch `fix/MONEY-1240`):** the same truncation pair
as MONEY-1240, in Ask Screener — and worse. **Modified**
`screener-chat-route.test.ts` (28 → **32**, no new file). `maxOutputTokens`
COUNTS the thinking budget, and this route pins `thinkingBudget: 512`, so at the
old cap of 1024 roughly half the allowance was gone before a single visible
character was produced. `finishReason` appeared in the file only inside a
comment about empty candidates and was never read, so the fragment rendered as a
finished reply. Cases mirror MONEY-1240 — `[regression]` MAX_TOKENS on a
text-only turn is a non-2xx error carrying no `text`; `[regression]` a truncated
turn is not charged; MAX_TOKENS alongside tool calls still returns 2xx so the
client's hop loop can finish an applied screen change — plus a budget assertion
that checks the REMAINDER (`cap - thinkingBudget >= 2048`) rather than the cap
alone, since the cap alone says nothing about how much room the answer has. The
pre-existing "pins an explicit thinking budget" case is untouched and still
guards the empty-candidate failure. Mutation-verified independently: dropping
the `finishReason` check fails 2, reverting the cap to 1024 fails 1.

**MONEY-1245 (2026-08-21, branch `fix/MONEY-1240`):** Ask FIRE and Ask Screener
kept their conversation only in a React `useRef`, so a refresh lost it and there
was nothing to see or delete. **+1 test file**
(`packages/services/__tests__/chat-history-tool-conversation.test.ts` **5** —
pure, no DB). The chats now save through the existing page-scoped `ChatHistory`
machinery, so `/chat-history`'s search / view / rename / archive / delete work
for them with no new UI; each panel also gets an in-panel list. Alongside the
transcript they persist `toolConversation` — the raw functionCall /
functionResponse turns — because a resume without them looks continuous to the
user while the model restarts blind to the plan or screen edits it already
applied. Kept OUT of `messages`, whose `{id, role, content, timestamp}` shape is
what /chat-history renders. The cases pin the field's dangerous property: it is
ABSENT (not null, not `[]`) on every pre-existing row AND on every StockSage
chat, since a Mongo `db push` creates indexes rather than fields — three
`[regression]` cases cover absent, null/undefined, and non-array values all
reading as "no tool context" without throwing, plus a round-trip and a case
asserting a StockSage row is indistinguishable from a legacy one so nobody
"backfills" it. That absent-vs-null class already caused MONEY-1050,
MONEY-1234 and MONEY-1235.

**MONEY-1246 / MONEY-1247 (2026-08-22, branch `fix/MONEY-1246`):** the
screener's "+ Add filter" button and every SUGGESTED chip did nothing, and all
six chips named filters the sidebar was already rendering a card for. **+1 test
file** (`apps/web/__tests__/screener/suggested-filter-chips.test.ts` **8** —
pure, no render). Both controls were wired to empty callbacks; the Add-filter
one is the nastier case, because `FilterSidebar` already guards it with
`disabled={!onAddFilter}` and an empty arrow function is TRUTHY, so passing one
DEFEATED the component's own guard and rendered the button enabled.

Worth recording how the tests got here: the first draft re-implemented both
rules inside the test file and passed 8/8 — **and passed identically with the
bug reintroduced**, because it was asserting its own copy. A textbook shadow
test, caught only by mutation. The fix was structural rather than test-side:
the chip list was a constant in one component while "is this filter set" was
duplicated across six `active` props, which is exactly why they drifted.
`components/screener/suggested-filters-logic.ts` now holds
`SUGGESTED_FILTERS`, `remainingSuggestions` and `deriveActiveFilterIds`, and
the component, the sidebar and the tests all execute that one implementation.
Cases: `[regression]` a chip hides once its filter is active; `[regression]`
nothing is offered when all six are in use (the section renders null rather
than an empty heading); `[regression]` a MIN-only bound counts as active; and
zero-is-a-real-bound, since `!= null` rather than truthiness is what stops a
deliberate `minDividendYield: 0` being re-suggested. Mutation-verified:
ignoring `activeIds` fails 3, swapping `!= null` for truthiness fails 1.

**MONEY-1253 follow-up (2026-08-27):** the fix above was correct and INVISIBLE.
**+1 test file** (`apps/web/__tests__/watchlist/membership-override-guard.test.ts`
**5** — source scan, no render).

`WatchlistPopover` publishes its member count to the parent on every change,
including the FIRST — but `lists` starts `[]`, so that first value is 0 and it
fires on MOUNT, before the popover has fetched anything (it only fetches when
opened). The cards apply it as `overrideCount ?? countFor(...)`, and `??` falls
through on null/undefined but NOT on 0. So the unfetched zero became a
PERMANENT override: every card read "+ Watch" and `countFor` was never
consulted again, even after membership loaded. Confirmed on a real account
whose cards should have read "In 2" / "In 1" / "In 1".

Gated on `cachedFor`, the popover's existing "I have fetched for this target"
marker, set only after a successful response — so a genuine 0 (last list
removed, or none) still publishes. One change covers both card types because
the popover is shared.

The scan pins four things: the early return; that `cachedFor` is set only on
success; that the effect DEPENDS on it (gating without the dep would latch and
never publish at all — the same blank screen by the opposite mistake); and that
both cards still use `??`, since switching one to `||` would discard a
legitimate 0 instead. No React harness exists in this repo, so the firing
conditions cannot be driven directly and a hand-rolled fake would only test
itself.

**MONEY-1253 (2026-08-24, branch `fix/MONEY-1240`):** every screener card
rendered "+ Watch" on load, including stocks already in three watchlists.
**+1 test file** (`apps/web/__tests__/watchlist/membership-count.test.ts`
**8** — pure, no DB, no render). Nothing was stale: `memberCount` was
`useState(0)` and only ever set by `WatchlistPopover.onMembershipChange`, which
fires when the popover OPENS, so membership was never fetched at all.

The fix had to be BATCHED. `getWatchlistsAction` already returns every list
with its `items`, so one cached call covers the whole page — and it must,
because the alternative is a request per card, which this screener has already
been burned by (mounting a ResearchModal per card "made the screener fan out a
server action per card on every refetch") on a page that refetches on every
filter change.

The counting rule lives in `lib/watchlist/membership-logic.ts` rather than
inside the hook, for two reasons: the hook is a "use client" file importing a
server action, so a node test could not reach the rule without dragging the
action in; and it must agree EXACTLY with `WatchlistPopover.deriveLists`, or
the closed trigger contradicts the popover it opens — the reported bug wearing
a different hat. Cases: `[regression]` the screenshot case (3 lists);
`[regression]` KIND scoping, since ETFs live under STOCK lists while MFs have
their own and counting across both would inflate every ETF card;
`[regression]` matching on exchange as well as symbol, so a dual-listed name
is not over-counted; a duplicate item within one list still counting that list
once; and null/undefined/empty reading as 0 rather than throwing, because
membership is decoration on a working page. Mutation-verified: dropping kind
scoping fails 1, matching on symbol alone fails 1.

**MONEY-1256 (2026-08-25, branch `fix/MONEY-1240`):** the side nav vanished on
first load for 13 routes. **+1 test file**
(`apps/web/__tests__/app/loading-keeps-sidebar.test.ts` **3** — walks `app/`).
The sidebar is rendered PER PAGE, not by the root layout, and deliberately so:
`Sidebar.tsx` records that one mount fires 19 middleware invocations at
550–1300 ms TTFB each. The consequence is that a route with no `loading.tsx`
renders NOTHING while the server responds — no chrome at all under the root
layout's topbar. All 49 existing loaders were fine (24 render `<Sidebar />`, 19
via `PageLoadingWrapper`, 6 via the paper-trading layout, which persists through
a nested loading boundary); the gap was routes with no loader.

The guard walks the real tree rather than asserting a list, since a list is
what fails to notice the next route added. Its first version was
MUTATION-CAUGHT as unfailable: `<Sidebar` also matches `<SidebarProvider>`,
which the ROOT layout renders, so the ancestor walk returned true for every
route and deleting a `loading.tsx` outright still passed. Tightened to
`<Sidebar[\s/>]`; the same mutation now fails and names the route.

**MONEY-1257 (2026-08-25, branch `fix/MONEY-1240`):** the tradebook TRADES tile
read "125" above "20 buys · 0 sells". **Modified**
`apps/web/__tests__/services/trades-logic-unit.test.ts` (57 → **61**, no new
file). The headline used the server `total` (every filtered trade) while the
split was derived CLIENT-side from one page of 100 — two populations rendered
as one fact. The "0 sells" is what made it harmful rather than untidy: it reads
as "you have never sold anything". `assembleTradeStats` now carries
`buyCount`/`sellCount`, counted server-side under the SAME `where` as
`totalTrades`, so the split sums to the headline for any filter; the demo path
derives them from the whole filtered set, never the page. Cases: `[regression]`
the split sums to `totalTrades`; omitted counts read 0 rather than a wrong
split; clamping (negative/NaN/fractional); and a sells-only account, the mirror
of the reported symptom. Mutation-verified: dropping the clamp fails 1.
**Composer "Reset all" (2026-08-21):** the popover footer's Reset-all button
shipped with NO `onClick` — a live-looking control that did nothing, the same
defect class as MONEY-1167's upload button. **+1 test file**
(`packages/services/__tests__/composer-reset-patch.test.ts` **7** — pure, no
DB): asserts the real exported `buildComposerResetPatch`, which the server
action calls. Three `[regression]` cases pin the quieter hazard the wiring
introduced — `setComposerPreferences` merges shallowly per namespace, so
resetting `sources` WHOLE would also write `webSearchUsedThisMonth: 0` and
`webSearchCap: 200`, turning Reset all into an unlimited free-quota button and
stamping a raised cap back to the default. Cases cover the patch carrying
neither key, a merge over a used allowance (57/1000 survives while `webSearch`
and `activeDocumentIds` clear), five repeated resets never refilling, and one
case documenting the trap by asserting the naive whole-namespace spread DOES
zero the meter. Mutation-verified: restoring the whole-namespace reset fails 3.
Also **modified** `apps/web/__tests__/actions/preferences-action.test.ts`
(8 → **9**): its per-action guard counts were literal `4`s, so the fifth action
failed them on arithmetic despite carrying all three guards. The counts now
DERIVE from the exported-action count, keeping the real invariant (one auth
check, one Unauthorized branch, one sanitized error per action) enforced at any
number of actions; the action names stay listed explicitly so a rename still
fails. Mutation-verified: stripping the new action's auth guard fails 2.

**MONEY-393 coverage-lift sections (§25-§41) - sub-90% files lifted to 90%+
(2026-05-12):**

These target individual source files c8 flagged below 90%. Pattern: install a
fake dependency (Redis / Prisma / IDB / ky / PostHog / Gemini) via
`require.cache` injection BEFORE importing the source, then walk the
previously-uncovered branches against a known-good stub. The `__esModule:true`
flag on stubs is load-bearing - without it, tsx's `__importDefault` interop
wraps the stub in an extra layer and the importer sees the wrong shape.

**§29 zerodha-client.ts (live data) — relocated to `workers/src/connect`
(MONEY-837); test is now `workers/__tests__/connect/zerodha-client.test.ts`. The
ESM-only-`ky` note below is retained as the rationale for the inline
reimplementation:**

`ky` is pure ESM (`"type": "module"` + `exports.default`), so the
`require.cache` injection used in §25-§28, §30, §32-§34 does NOT intercept the
ESM loader. Without a custom Node `--import` hook, the HTTP-bound
`getZerodhaQuote` / `getZerodhaQuotes` / `getZerodhaHistorical` paths can't be
cleanly mocked. The existing `__tests__/market/zerodha-client.test.ts` (38
cases, inline reimplementation of the helpers) is what's keeping the 36% floor.
Lifting this would require:

1. A `--import=./test-loader.mjs` Node hook that intercepts `ky` resolution at
   the ESM layer, OR
2. Extracting the response-transformation logic into pure helpers (refactor)

Neither is in scope for MONEY-393. Marked deferred.

**§42 Final coverage gate - accepted with cardinality bounds:**

c8 instrumentation hangs on Gemini-instrumented test files (5+ files), so a
clean `yarn test:coverage` sweep across `apps/web` is not runnable without
excluding those. The replacement gate: full `yarn test` (no c8) green via turbo
pipes; 509 test files, ~19,829 test cases, 100% pass. Component files
(terminal-luxe primitives, SipCalculator) have an inherent ceiling around 40-50%
because their React-render branches require a DOM that node:test doesn't
provide - this is documented per-section above. The lift sections (§25-§41) each
hit ≥90% on the targeted file when run in isolation under c8.

**Vercel preview build unblocked (2026-05-12, commit `6b73e9fe`):**

`apps/web/lib/security/oauth-state.ts` was importing
`import logger from "@/lib/logger"` - but `@/lib/logger` is a factory function
(returns a Logger), not a Logger instance. `tsc --noEmit` accepted it because
the factory IS a valid imported value; Next.js's build catches `logger.warn` on
the un-called factory and errors. Switched to
`import { authLogger as logger } from "@usemoney/logger"` (the canonical
pre-bound Logger instance pattern, matching apps/web/lib/gemini/\*.ts and
others). Build now passes in 52s. New rule recorded in memory: **for any
source-code change in a multi-commit bundle, `yarn build` is mandatory** -
type-check alone is not equivalent.

**MONEY-287 - OAuth CSRF state across 7 broker callbacks + tests (2026-05-12):**

| Test File                                                  | Cases | Covers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| _(moved, MONEY-1062)_ `oauth-state{,-ttl,-source}.test.ts` | —     | Module moved to `packages/core/src/brokers/oauth-state.ts`; suites superseded by `packages/core/__tests__/brokers/oauth-state.test.ts` (19). The web copies' `@/lib/redis` cache-injection could not retarget the core redis seam, so they were folded rather than repointed. |

Source-side: new `apps/web/lib/security/oauth-state.ts` with
`generateOAuthState`, `verifyOAuthState`, `__peekOAuthStateForTests`. Redis
`SET … EX 600 NX` for atomic write; `DEL` returns 1 on first verify, 0 on
replay - single-use enforced at Redis level, race-free across concurrent
callbacks. `apps/web/lib/actions/broker-connection.ts:getOAuthUrlAction` mints a
state per (userId, broker) and appends `?state=…` to each authorization URL
(Fyers uses its native `state` arg); `handleOAuthCallbackAction` verifies the
state and rejects mismatches with a generic user-facing error. Soft-fail when
state is missing during the migration window - set `OAUTH_STATE_STRICT=1` once
all 7 round-trips are verified in prod. 7 callback routes updated to extract +
forward `state` (Zerodha, Upstox, Fyers, Angel One, ICICI, HDFC, Interactive
Brokers). Groww + Dhan are not OAuth and are excluded.

MONEY-1131 identity proof — the sector pushdown is differential, not
re-implemented: the same fixture runs through a DB double that HONOURS the new
clause and one that IGNORES it (i.e. pre-change behaviour) and the results must
`deepEqual`. The JS `sectorMatches` pass is deliberately RETAINED after the
pushdown, so the DB clause can only ever be equal-or-looser and provably cannot
change the visible set. Mutation-checked: deleting the retained JS pass fails 2
cases, an off-by-one in the page slice fails 2 more.

Cache keys were deliberately NOT bumped. `main-v3` has a 24h TTL and no
invalidator, so bumping it would make the first request after every deploy pay a
full-collection scan — worse than the parse being removed. The four new keys are
additive and warm on first miss.

The defect it is written against: `toYahooSymbol` suffixes anything that is not BSE with `.NS`, so `DOW` on NASDAQ becomes `DOW.NS` — a REAL NSE symbol for a DIFFERENT company — and Yahoo answers it, producing a confident wrong price rather than an error. Both lines of defence are asserted: the US chain contains no Yahoo provider, AND `yahooQuoteProvider` REFUSES a US venue when handed one directly (a chain is data, and data can be assembled wrongly). Also pins `isPublic:false` on the Tiingo provider — Commercial licence is internal-use-only, so those quotes must never enter the cross-user `_global` cache. Mutation-verified: dropping the US branch from `resolveQuoteChain` → 1 red                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `__tests__/market/us-quote-freshness.test.ts`   | 15    | `app/api/market/quote/quote-logic.ts#isLiveQuote` + the quote route + `components/market/DelayedDataNote.tsx` + `apps/api/src/routes/v1/market.ts` (MONEY-1309 T9, rewritten by the follow-up). ONE function decides what "live" means and all FOUR surfaces read it — independent re-derivations are how MONEY-1259 hid a compliance disclosure. **This file previously MISSED the defect it covered**: it tested a SOURCE-ONLY predicate and then source-scanned the consumers for the literal `isLiveQuoteSource(source)`, pinning the very expression that was incomplete, while `DelayedDataNote` rendered a fallback quote as live. The predicate now takes the PROVENANCE, the matrix includes `{TIINGO_RT, fallback:true}`, and the rendered-output half moved to `us-quote-live-badge.test.ts`. What stays here is the wiring claim, which IS structural: the shared function is core's own (identity-asserted, not a look-alike), no source-only predicate remains exported, and apps/api calls it rather than hand-writing the condition. Mutation-verified: re-hardcoding `delayed: true` → 1 red; apps/api re-deriving by hand → 1 red |

Source scan, named as the weaker instrument it is. MONEY-1128 de-shadow — `atlas-search.test.ts` was a SHADOW: it re-declared
`isAtlasSearchError`, the latch and all three pipeline builders inline and
asserted its own copies, so it tested nothing that shipped. Worse, it asserted
`PlanExecutor -> unavailable`, the exact behaviour MONEY-1128 removed, and kept
passing. 52 -> 32 cases: the latch/classifier suites were deleted (covered for
real by `search-atlas-gate.test.ts`), and the pipeline suites now import the real
exported builders. The shadow copies were also WRONG about what ships — they
asserted a flat `text` clause where the real pipeline is a nested
`compound.should` with four match strategies. Mutation-proved: 15 deliberate
breaks injected, 15 caught.

MONEY-1148 de-shadow — `stock-formatters.test.ts`'s `formatMarketCap` block
asserted the implementation rather than reality. The T and B divisors were each
10x too large ("T" divided by 1e13, "B" by 1e10), and the tests encoded that:
one case was named "Reliance market cap (~17T INR)" while asserting `"₹1.75 T"`,
with a comment rationalising the gap as "B unit = 1000 Crore = 10 billion".
Tests written FROM an implementation can only ever confirm it.

The expectations were rewritten, not adjusted until green, and the convention
was decided first: lakh-crore, converging on `formatMarketCapCrores` so the
stock header, the Fundamentals card and Discover all read from ONE ladder.
`formatMarketCap` now converts rupees and delegates; the T/B ladder is deleted
rather than repaired. Reliance renders `₹17.50 L Cr`.

Two of the new cases are structural rather than point assertions. One pins
MONOTONICITY across the buckets — the old ladder printed "T" from two branches
dividing by different constants, so ₹9.9e12 read "₹9.90 T" while ₹1.0e13 read
"₹1.00 T" and the figure shrank as the company grew; asserting the ordering
makes that whole class impossible. The other asserts `formatMarketCap(r) ===
formatMarketCapCrores(r / 1e7)`, so if the two surfaces ever diverge again the
suite fails instead of users noticing.

Sibling swept in the same change: `app/discover/client.tsx` carried a verbatim
copy of the buggy ladder (identical divisors, `.toFixed(1)`), feeding the
Discover stock list and the ETF AUM label. Both its callers pass rupees, so it
now delegates to the shared formatter instead of remaining a second copy.

NOT swept, deliberately: `packages/research/src/tools/compute-sector-aggregates.ts`
has its own `formatMarketCap`, but it is a different function over a
caller-supplied unit (a tool argument), and its "Lakh Cr" threshold looks wrong
by a different factor. Guessing at its intended unit is how the original defect
was introduced; it needs its own ticket.

**MONEY-1274 gate find (2026-08-29)** — `period-start-clamp.test.ts`, 7 cases.
The full gate went red on `yahoo-client-helpers.test.ts` ("6 months ago for
'6mo'": `2 !== 1`) — NOT a regression from this branch, a latent CALENDAR flake
that fires only on the 29th-31st. `getPeriodStartDate` did
`setMonth(getMonth() - 6)`, which keeps the day, so on 29 Aug it asked for
29 Feb 2026; that date does not exist and JS Date rolls forward to 1 MARCH. A
"6 month" chart window was a month short on those days, and "1y" from 29 Feb
started on 1 March. No error, and the chart still rendered.

Fixed with a clamped `monthsBack` helper (move to the 1st, shift the month, then
clamp the day to the target month's length). BOTH copies of the ladder route
through it — `historical-fetcher.ts` carried the identical defect, and repairing
one while leaving the other is how two copies drift apart.

The new cases are DATE-INDEPENDENT: the existing tests call
`getPeriodStartDate()`, which reads `new Date()` internally, so they can only
fail on the days the bug happens to fire. These pin the pure helper against
fixed dates, plus a sweep over every day of a 31-day month × 1/3/6/12 months
asserting the result never lands outside the target month — the assertion that
would have caught this on ANY calendar day.

MONEY-1137 — demo state must never survive an authenticated session. The core
property (stale localStorage flag + signed-in user ⇒ false) is pinned for both
the `useUser()` object and the `useAuth().userId` string forms, with a
`[regression]` case holding the old `true`. Signed-out + flag still ⇒ true, so
real demo visitors are unaffected. Includes a repo-wide walk of
`app/ components/ hooks/ lib/` asserting EVERY `useIsDemoMode(...)` passes
`user` — with a `>= 30` call-site floor so it cannot pass vacuously (the
MONEY-1093 lesson), plus four `@ts-expect-error` directives pinning that the
un-gated form no longer compiles. An unused `@ts-expect-error` is itself a
compile error, so those fail loudly if the unsafe form ever returns.

This matters beyond banners: `isDemoMode` also swaps in fabricated data —
`FundCompositionSection` renders invented holdings and weights with no banner at
all, and `app/discover/client.tsx` sets mock data AND `skip: true` on all four
real fetches. A stale flag there showed a paying user a wholly fictional page.

MONEY-1128 — the classifier splits errors by DETERMINISM, not severity: will the
next request fail identically regardless of cluster health? Only then may the
5-minute process-wide fallback latch. `PlanExecutor`/timeout names the LOCATION
of a failure, not the diagnosis — latching on it turned a loaded cluster into a
guaranteed load spiral, because the regex fallback is a double collection scan.
Unrecognised errors are rethrown: a silent fallback on an unknown error is how
the original defect stayed hidden.

MONEY-1127 — `redis-singleton` pins the cold-start single-flight (N concurrent
`getRedisClient()` calls construct exactly ONE client), dispose-before-replace,
the bounded retry ladder replacing the old permanent-null dead end, and four
fail-open paths. `memory-ttl` pins the per-module L1 policy: modules WITH a live
invalidator get a short `memoryTtl`; the multi-MB 24h `discover` blobs and the
no-invalidator modules deliberately do NOT (a short L1 there would re-fetch and
re-parse megabytes to obtain byte-identical data). Also covers the L2→L1
promotion re-stamp — promoted entries previously inherited the LRU's 5-minute
default regardless of config.

MONEY-1092 — single-flight + stale-while-error. Two entries per logical key: a
short-TTL served copy and a long-TTL last-known-good one, so a failed recompute
degrades instead of blanking the surface. Ports-injected, so the whole state
machine is exercised with in-memory fakes and no Redis. The `isPermanentError`
port exists because a permanent answer ("this sector has no instruments") must
NOT be masked by a 24h-old copy — stale-fallback is for outages only.

Two of the 18 cover `cachedWithStaleFallback`, the BOUND helper, rather than the
state machine. They exist because unit-testing the state machine was not enough:
a revision destructured `isPermanentError` from the args and never forwarded it
into the ports object, so callers passing a classifier silently got default
behaviour. Every unit test still passed, and so did a mutation test on the guard
— both exercise the layer that was correct. A guard proven to work in isolation
is not a guard proven to be REACHED.

MONEY-1205 added the nine rows above. Each pins a defect that produced a
CONFIDENT WRONG value rather than an error: `csv-line` is the RFC-4180 splitter
extracted so `zerodha-instruments-logic.ts`'s `line.split(",")` (13,287 of 26,669
prod instrument names stored WITH their literal quotes) cannot be re-copied;
`fund-composition-provenance` pins that freshness is gated on the disclosure
MONTH, not on `extractedAt`, which re-arms itself on every re-extraction and can
therefore never fire; `mf-nav-cold-read`'s load-bearing assertion is the NEGATIVE
one — `globalThis.fetch` is never called on a read; `xbrl-units` pins the
₹-to-crore conversion AND that converting does not defeat `reconcile()`'s
`SCALE_MISMATCH` block, which is the only thing standing between a units bug and
an irreversible write into a table with no `source` in its unique key.

MONEY-1125 — the batched-candle rewrite. Output identity is asserted against a
verbatim port of the OLD per-instrument loops over the same fixture, so the test
fails if batching changes any result. Query-count guards pin the N+1 out (250
instruments ⇒ exactly `ceil(250/100)` calls, never one-per-instrument) along with
the query shape (`in` list ≤ chunk, `orderBy` `[{instrumentId},{date}]`, no
DB-side `take`). **The `take: 300` + `date: "asc"` window — which selects the
OLDEST 300 candles, not the newest — is pinned deliberately: it is a pre-existing
bug tracked as MONEY-1133, and this test is its tripwire. Changing that ordering

MONEY-1205 added five of the rows above; MONEY-1209 added `log-boundary`.

`ownership-shp-xbrl-bse` is the only place the two NEW ownership legs are
exercised end-to-end, and every fixture in it is CAPTURED: the 19,386-byte
all-zero body `api.bseindia.com` returns for a nonexistent scripcode AND a
nonexistent qtrid (identical for both — that combination IS the trap), a real
`shareholding_patterns.raw` XBRL URL, and the `-` sentinel NSE emits for a filing
with no XBRL. A synthetic fixture written to the same guess as the code cannot
falsify the guess, which is how `public_val` stayed unmapped across 7,953 prod
rows while the older suite was green.

`mf-metadata-cursor-db` is the one test here that needs a server, and
deliberately so: Prisma + MongoDB does NOT match an **absent** field with
`{ field: null }`, so no pure test can catch it — `{ metadataSyncedAt: null }`
selected 7,263 of 14,223 prod rows and missed the 6,960 that had never been
touched. It runs the OLD clause too and asserts it selects only one of the two
otherwise-identical documents, so the mutation proof travels with the test. Gated
by `RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=true` (+ `DATABASE_URL`) like `tests/integration/db/**`;
un-gated it reports 1 skipped-placeholder case. Writes are confined to
`ZZTEST-MONEY1205-` scheme codes and removed in `after()`, including on failure.

### 10. Other Tested Areas

#### Log-payload redaction (MONEY-1209)

Three files, one leak, three independent paths to a log sink. NSE session
cookies (`ak_bmsc`, `bm_mi`, `bm_sz`) were reaching prod Cloud Logging in
plaintext because a ky/got/axios error carries the credentialed request on its
own enumerable properties, and `console.error("[job] failed:", err)` prints
them.

| Source File                                                    | Test File                                            | Test Cases | Status |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------ |
| `packages/utils/src/log-redaction.ts`                          | `packages/utils/__tests__/log-redaction.test.ts`     | 18         | PASS   |
| `workers/src/log-boundary.ts` (+ `index.ts`)                   | `workers/__tests__/log-boundary.test.ts`             | 10         | PASS   |
| `packages/logger/src/config.ts` (serializers + `redact.paths`) | `packages/logger/__tests__/config-redaction.test.ts` | 12         | PASS   |

Every case asserts the RENDERED output (`util.inspect` at `depth: null` for the
console path, the real bytes pino writes for the logger path) rather than the
returned object, because inspect's default depth of 2 hides deep nodes that a
JSON sink still publishes in full. Every secret also carries a CONTROL assertion
proving the unredacted value leaks through the same rendering path — without it
a case can pass because the leak never existed in that shape.

15 mutants were run against these suites and all 15 died: removing the
`installLogRedaction()` call from the entry point, disabling the string scanner,
the key rule, the cycle guard, the depth budget and the `Request`/`Headers`
flattening; returning the live object instead of plain data; unwrapping either
pino serializer; wrapping only `console.error`; dropping the idempotency guard;
and passing console args through unredacted. The key-rule mutant initially
SURVIVED the workers suite — the ticket's own payload (`cookie:
"ak_bmsc=..."`) is covered twice over, by key AND by value shape, so it cannot
tell the two rules apart. `[boundary] redacts an opaque credential only the key
rule can catch` was added for exactly that gap.

MONEY-1205 added the four rows above. `discover-search-casing` pins an
asymmetry, not a rule: the `instrument_search` index maps `symbol` as
`lucene.keyword` (one unmodified token), so only an exactly-cased symbol scores
on the `text` leg — measured on prod, `"sbin"` ranked SBIN 5th and `"SBIN"`
ranked it 1st. So the instrument ATLAS query is uppercased, the Prisma fallback
is NOT (it is genuinely case-insensitive via `mode:"insensitive"`), and the MF
Atlas query is NOT (that index uses `lucene.standard` for the name fields).
Asserting only "the file contains `.toUpperCase()`" would pass with any of the
three wrong, so each is located and checked at its own call site.
`fund-nav-derivatives-service`'s load-bearing case is the cache rule: a COLD read
has just queued the backfill that fixes it, so caching "we have nothing" would
turn a transient gap into a shift-long one.

MONEY-705 — the stampede tests assert the **literal cache-key strings on the
wire** (recorded through a fake Redis, not re-derived with the same helper) so a
refactor cannot silently orphan entries written by the deployed version, plus an
end-to-end case where a value seeded via the OLD public API is served by the new
path. Five concurrent-A/B cases cover the one catastrophic failure available
here — two users collapsing onto one flight. The XIRR file pins bit-identity
under the 50k row cap against a frozen clock, and the honest "—" above it;
`take: 50_001` and the absence of a date floor are both asserted, because a date
floor would silently change a money-weighted return the user is shown.

##### MONEY-620 live-money-service hardening (`*-logic.ts` units + `*-poison-live` + `*-service-e2e`)

The MONEY-620 epic extracted the pure decision logic out of ~21 services into
exported `packages/services/src/*-logic.ts` modules and added three test shapes
per surface: a **`-logic-unit`** suite (drives the real exported pure helper),
a **`-poison-live`** suite (feeds adversarial/poisoned upstream rows — NaN,
negative qty, cross-user ids, mixed currency, stale ticks — and asserts the
service fails closed / sanitizes), and a **`-service-e2e`** suite (drives the
real service through a recording-prisma seam). ~159 bugs were surfaced and fixed.

A declared topic that nothing publishes to is invisible: the infra scripts create
it, a processor and a route consume it, the docs list a trigger — and it never
fires. Nothing errors and nothing is logged. This guard requires every entry in
`PUBSUB_TOPICS` to have EITHER a code publisher (`getTopicName(...)` handed to
`client.topic(...)`) or a `SCHEDULER_DEFS` line in `setup-scheduler.sh`; test
files are excluded from the scan, because a topic whose only publisher is a test
is exactly the dead topic being looked for. Two were found and deleted in
MONEY-1205 — `fund-composition-sync` (so composition refresh was 100%
page-view-driven: a user opening an ETF page WAS the cron) and
`proactive-analysis` (declared and topic-created with no publisher, route or
processor at all).

MONEY-1130 — `/` now SERVES the marketing landing instead of client-redirecting
to `/home`. The redirect was not merely slow: `robots.ts` allows `/` and
DISALLOWS `/home`, so it pointed crawlers at a robots-disallowed URL and the
homepage could not be indexed at all. Tests pin that `/` reads no per-request
state (so it stays prerendered), that middleware owns the signed-in decision,
and — after a shallow-merge bug was found in the BUILT html — every OpenGraph
field individually, because a page-level `openGraph` silently REPLACES the
layout's rather than merging it.

MONEY-1132 — the sidebar's 19 `<Link>`s all prefetched on viewport entry, and
because every destination is `force-dynamic` WITH a `loading.tsx`, each prefetch
is a real server round trip through a 462KB Node middleware doing Clerk `auth()`.
`NavContent` re-mounts per navigation, so the burst repeated. The eager set was
chosen from 90 days of PostHog pageviews (785 total), not intuition: a 3.5x cliff
at 28 -> 8 pageviews splits it, keeping 94% of the instant-navigation benefit for
42% of the requests. Hover/focus prefetch is re-added by hand because Next gates
those handlers on the same `prefetch` prop.

MONEY-1144 — `vendor-labels-hidden` pins a distinction that is easy to get wrong
in BOTH directions. Removed: the "TICKERTAPE" pill (rendered `data.source`
straight from the row) and the chart's "Yahoo" pill — labels naming who we get
data FROM. Kept, and asserted as kept so the rule is not over-applied: "Zerodha"
on the same chart pill (that is the USER'S broker, and it means the chart is
live rather than delayed), the `screener.in`/`tickertape.in` citation favicons
in chat/research (citing a source you read is attribution), and the competitor
tables on the marketing pages. It also covers the second half of the ticket —
`StockRatios.marketCap` is in CRORES, and formatting it with the RUPEES
formatter divided by 1e7 twice and rendered every mid-cap as a confident
"₹0 Cr" rather than an empty state.

MONEY-1255 — that same unit bug then shipped a SECOND time, on the Peers table
of the same page, and this file is why it is now covered. `StockPeersTab` had a
file-LOCAL `fmtMcap` doing `const cr = v / 1e7` on a value already in crores, so
APOLLOTYRE's ₹28,023 Cr rendered "₹0 Cr" — every row, every company. Being
file-local is what let it live: `stock-formatters.test.ts` covered the shared
pair exhaustively and could not import this one at all. The guard is therefore
scoped to the RULE (a list of surfaces that render a crores market cap), not to
one file — the lesson MONEY-1207 wrote down — and asserts the code SHAPE: import
the shared formatter, never the rupees one, and re-derive no `/ 1e7` locally.

The rupees formatter was fixed in the same pass (MONEY-1148). It carried its own
T/B ladder with two wrong rungs: "B" divided by 1e10, and TWO trillion rungs made
it NON-MONOTONIC — crossing ₹10 T dropped the displayed figure from "₹9.90 T" to
"₹1.00 T", so Reliance read "₹1.75 T" for ₹17.5 trillion. Every assertion in the
old test block pinned that output, two of them with a comment rationalising the
error into a convention, which is exactly why a green suite hid it. Per D-b the
function now converts to crores and delegates to `formatMarketCapCrores` — one
ladder, no second place to drift — and `stock-formatters.test.ts` gained a
MONOTONICITY SWEEP, because the defect was invisible at any single value
("₹9.90 T" and "₹1.00 T" are each plausible) and only existed in the RELATION
between adjacent inputs.

MONEY-1145 — `stock-tabs-natural-key` pins the read key for the stock tabs.
`instrumentId` is a MUTABLE denormalised FK; re-seeding `instrument_mappings`
re-mints ObjectIds and silently orphans every dependent row. Measured on the dev
DB before the fix: **0 of 32,359 `StockFinancials` rows were reachable** by
instrumentId (2,123 symbols), so the Financials tab was empty for every stock on
the platform while the data sat there the whole time. Reading the DECLARED
natural key — `@@unique([symbol, exchange, statementType, periodType, period])`,
the same key the writer upserts on — recovers all 2,123 symbols and cannot
re-orphan, which an id-repair migration would (it fixes today and breaks at the
next re-seed). The file also guards the OPPOSITE mistake: `dailyPrice` is
genuinely instrument-keyed (`@@unique([instrumentId, date])`, no symbol column)
and its rows are NOT orphaned, because the price sync re-resolves ids daily.

MONEY-1142 — `premium-actions-gated` closes a client-only paywall. `/risk`,
`/tax`, `/documents`, `/strategies` and `/quizzes` enforced their tier ONLY in
the client `PageGuard`; the actions behind them checked authentication and
nothing else, and a server action is invocable directly. Reachable in practice
via the MONEY-1137 demo-flag bypass. The durable half is the `[completeness]`
case: it walks `PAGE_TO_FEATURE_MAP` and fails when a premium route has no
asserted gate, so the NEXT premium feature cannot ship ungated by omission —
mutation-proved by adding a fake premium route. Exemptions live in `KNOWN_GAPS`
and must name what enforces the route instead, with a test that the named
mechanism still exists (`/sage-tutor` is quota-metered in `/api/chat`, not
gated).

MONEY-1149 — `/learning`'s feature mismatch, previously carried here as a
`[known gap]`, is now RESOLVED and the gap case is replaced by three that pin
the resolution (13 → 15 cases). The map named `learningContent` for the route,
so `PageGuard` blocked FREE users, while the lesson TEXT behind it was gated
only by `advancedCourses` (ADVANCED content only) — a FREE caller could read
any BASIC/INTERMEDIATE lesson in full via the server action while being bounced
from the page that renders exactly that content.

Resolved in favour of the CODE: the map entry is `null`, matching `/analysis`
and `/discover` after MONEY-394, and matching middleware, which already had
`/learning(.*)` in `PUBLIC_ROUTE_PATTERNS` — `PageGuard` was the lone dissenter.

The precise reading matters, and "learningContent is unenforced" is the
tempting WRONG summary: it is enforced, just not on this surface.
`/api/storage/stream` checks it before serving any non-document path, so
premium lesson videos and PDFs stay PREMIUM/ULTIMATE-only whatever the page map
says. One of the new cases pins exactly that, because it is the assumption that
makes opening the page safe — if that gate ever goes, ungating the page turns
from a funnel decision into giving away the premium media. A third case is an
escape hatch rather than a lock: re-gating `/learning` is a legitimate product
decision, but doing it by restoring the map entry ALONE recreates the leak, so
that case fails unless `learning-logic.ts` enforces the newly-named feature
too. The assertion binds to the imported `PAGE_TO_FEATURE_MAP`, not to a
re-parse of its source text.

MONEY-1146 — `shareholding-failure-visible` pins the distinction between a
FAILED fetch and a genuinely empty one. The action used to `catch` everything
and return `{ success: true, shareholding: [] }`, so a blocked scrape, a
rate-limit, a vendor layout change and an uncovered symbol all rendered the
same empty panel — the failure mode where a dead feature is indistinguishable
from a working one. `StockShareholdingTab` had an error branch the whole time
(`:73-77`); it was simply unreachable. The file also guards the OVER-correction
(a real empty answer must stay `success: true`, or every uncovered stock shows
a red panel), that the empty/failed answer is never cached, and that the DB read
precedes the scrape. The `apps/api` parity test that asserted the old behaviour
— literally named _"SWALLOWS a fetch error → success with empty (quirk)"_ — was
rewritten, not patched.

Note the `[meta]` case in `scans-hidden-from-nav`: its `stripComments` helper must
remove LINE comments BEFORE block comments. `Sidebar.tsx` has a `//` comment
containing `tours/*`, whose `/*` otherwise opens a phantom block that eats 11,192
characters — measured. It swallows no `href:` today, so probing a live nav entry
would NOT detect it; the ordering is therefore tested directly, on input that
reproduces it.

MONEY-1138 — the two halves pull in opposite directions, which is why both are
pinned. Scans must be gone from EVERY navigation surface (sidebar, and the ⌘K
palette transitively, since `CommandPalette` iterates the exported
`sidenavConfig` — asserted, not assumed), for every user including the founder.
But `/discover/scans` must NOT be added to `FORCE_DISABLED_ROUTES`: that is
/paper-trading's mechanism and it closes the ROUTE too, locking the founder out
of a page they are still building. Getting half of it right looks correct in a
screenshot and is wrong in both directions.

MONEY-1126 — these are gate tests before they are perf tests. `guards-wiring`
pins that only the NON-blocking answer is ever reused (a ghosted session or an
unaccepted-terms answer is re-asked on every navigation, exactly as before) and
that a rejected call is never remembered. `entitlement-isolation` pins the
separation that matters most: `PageGuard` / `useSubscriptionAccess` must never
read the localStorage-backed `plan-cache`, whose own header documents that its
value "can belong to whoever was previously signed in on this browser" — reading
it for a gating decision would let a previous PREMIUM user's plan admit a FREE
user. `access-cache` pins that an error-path `DEFAULT_FREE_ACCESS` is NEVER
written, so a transient DB blip cannot pin a paying user to FREE for the TTL.

MONEY-1123 — the module-scoped result LRU (cap 50, 60s TTL, injected clock) that
stops a backspace from re-issuing a query the browser just answered. Covers
recency refresh on read, eviction past the cap, TTL expiry, and key composition
(query + limit + includeIndices + types) so two different option sets cannot
collide on one entry.

MONEY-1084 — PostHog passed `capture_pageview: true`, posthog-js's LEGACY
load-only mode, so in an App Router SPA every client-side route change was
invisible: 475 pageviews across 441 prod sessions over 14 days (~1.08 each).
That is why a reproducible navigation bug (MONEY-1082) left no trace in
analytics, and why any funnel spanning more than one route was measuring
landings only. Static scan on the init config — the value lives in a client
component with nothing callable, and the failure mode is exactly "someone sets
it back to `true`". Mutation-tested. Note `defaults: "2025-05-24"` already
resolved this correctly; the explicit `true` was overriding a good default.

| `core/market-data/instruments/sector-write-guard.ts` + all 4 unattended sector writers (discovered)         | `market-data/sector-write-guard.test.ts`            | 15         | PASS   |
| `core/market-data/instruments/sector-key-match.ts` + 5 consumers (planner, rotation, health, macro, stress) | `market-data/sector-key-match.test.ts`              | 12         | PASS   |
| `workers/processors/bhavcopy-sync-logic.ts` (metadata plan)                                                 | `workers/bhavcopy-metadata-backfill.test.ts`        | 51         | PASS   |
| `core/market-data/instruments/zerodha-instruments.ts` (`mapToUpdate`) + `instrument-sync.ts` call site      | `market-data/instrument-provider-authority.test.ts` | 19         | PASS   |
| `core/market-data/instruments/bse-master-logic.ts`                                                          | `market-data/bse-master-logic.test.ts`              | 50         | PASS   |

Two of these files guard the parts that a fresh-context review caught, not the
parts that were designed up front. `instrument-provider-authority.test.ts`
covers a nightly collision: `instrument-sync` (22:00 IST, every day) rewrote
`series` and `instrumentType` from Kite's dump one hour after `bhavcopy-sync`
(21:00 IST, weekdays) wrote the real exchange values — so the whole pipeline
below was inert, silently, with no error. Its last describe block reads the
`instrument-sync.ts` call site directly, because on MONEY-1092 a fix shipped
that was correct as a unit and never actually invoked.

`InstrumentMapping` held 22,090 active EQUITY rows of which **11,795 were
actually debt** — 8.85% Piramal bonds, IRFC bonds, NHAI bonds, G-Secs — because
the instrument master is built from the Zerodha dump, which types every cash
instrument `EQ`. Worse, ~2,200 of them carried a real sector: `0795GOI32`, a GOI
bond, labelled "Financial Services".

**A symbol-pattern matcher cannot do this job**, and the tests exist mostly to
pin that. The candidate regex `^\d+[A-Z]+\d{2}[A-Z]?$` hit 2,236 wrong rows and
recalled only 2,752 of 11,795: real equities begin with digits (`3MINDIA`,
`5PAISA`, `63MOONS`, `1STCUS`, `3PLAND`) and real bonds do not always look like
bonds (`EPDPGSEC28`, `CSAI240226`). The pattern correlates with the truth
without being it — which is the worst property a heuristic can have, because it
survives casual testing.

The real signal is the exchange's own settlement series, which both exchanges
publish daily and `bhavcopy.ts` already parsed into `BhavcopyRow.series` — it
was simply never persisted. Measured on the live 2026-07-29 BSE file: group `F`
(369 rows) and `G` (43) are debt, the other 4,433 across A/B/X/XT/T/M/MT/Z/E/
IF/P/MS are equity, and 408 of those 412 F/G rows carry a non-equity ISIN type —
two independent signals agreeing. The NSE half REUSES `NSE_CASH_SERIES` /
`NSE_SERIES_INTENTIONALLY_UNPRICED` / `NSE_SERIES_FAMILIES_UNPRICED` from
`bhavcopy.ts` rather than re-listing them, so the price feed and the classifier
cannot drift.

**BSE uses an ALLOW-list, and that choice cost a bug.** The first version used
only the debt deny-list and treated everything else as equity. But
`InstrumentMapping.series` defaults to the stamped string `"EQ"`, which BSE never
issues as a group — so the deny-list returned a confident EQUITY for 12,661 BSE
rows whose real group was unknown. A wrong default is more dangerous than a
missing value because no null check catches it. Caught by running the repair
script's dry-run against live prod, not by a unit test.

Also covered: both un-normalising sector writers. `screener/engine.ts`
`backfillMissingSectors` wrote raw Yahoo GICS on EVERY fundamental screener
request, and `enrich-sectors-gemini.ts` declared its own 18-value vocabulary
(seven names not in the taxonomy) plus an "Other" escape hatch — together the
source of prod's Other (228), Construction (40), Real Estate (19), Media &
Entertainment (9) and Agriculture (5). Repairing the data alone would have been
undone on the next screener run. The alias-coverage test also caught `Realty`
mapping nowhere, silently becoming its own unfilterable bucket.

All guards mutation-tested.
