MONEY-1217 — `deep-dive-results-calendar.test.ts` re-inverts the hidden-state
assertions MONEY-1218 left behind: the earnings calendar was commented out
because it rendered a 30-day month grid with a green "0 events" pill for
essentially every sector, which reads as "this sector has no earnings this
month". The scans now assert the calendar RENDERS, that the count pill is
guarded on `total > 0`, that the query is bounded by a results SEASON rather
than `now + 30 days`, and that both scopes (sector / stock) are reachable. It
keeps two schema canaries — `UpcomingEvent.symbol` stays nullable (macro events
have no issuer, so the loader's filter must stay live) and
`InstrumentMapping.eventsSyncedAt` exists (the rotation marker that stops
events-sync re-fetching the same slice of the widened warm tier every night).
The BEHAVIOUR it depends on — season boundaries, FY rollover, leap day, and the
omission of zero-event days — is unit-tested against the real functions in
`packages/core/__tests__/market-data/results-season.test.ts` (31 cases).

MONEY-1092 — `/discover/sectors` intermittently rendered "Failed to load
market heatmap", and a picked sector could hang on a spinner forever. Root
cause was a **missing index**: `LatestQuote` declared only `[changePercent]`
and `[instrumentId, changePercent]`, while the heatmap sorts
`orderBy: { marketCap: "desc" }` over the collection — so MongoDB ran a
blocking in-memory SORT before `take` applied. Three amplifiers: no
single-flight (an expiring 60s key let every concurrent visitor launch its
own 3000-row scan), no SSR priming on the sectors page, and a catch block
that collapsed every cause into one generic string.

`slug.test.ts` pins the "NORMALIZE on write, RESOLVE BY LOOKUP on read"
contract for `?sector=` deep links. The regression it exists for: the old
route did `slug.replace(/-/g, " ")`, which turns "Consumer Non-Durables"
into a sector that does not exist. Round-trips all 12 canonical NSE
sectors plus the sentinel and passthrough buckets through real
`URLSearchParams` encoding. Mutation-tested — restoring the reverse
transform turns 6 red.

`heatmap-buckets.test.ts` pins both halves of the bucket-label contract:
`"N/A"` (the `SECTOR_SKIPPED` enrichment sentinel) remaps to
"Not Categorised" to match the four other surfaces that already did, while
non-canonical passthrough buckets ("Other", "Agriculture", …) stay visible
and unchanged — folding those in would hide a real data problem and shift
every m-cap weight in the ranked table. Mutation-tested (2 red).

`deep-dive-query-shape.test.ts` is a static scan (same pattern as
`no-unguarded-url-writes.test.ts`) because these are invariants of a
`"use server"` action talking to Prisma — untestable without a database, but
very much deletable by a future edit. All three pins were measured against
live prod:

- **Exchange filter.** `sector-deep-dive.ts` had NO exchange filter, so
  `{EQUITY, isActive, sector}` matched **4,394** rows for Financial Services
  (BSE 4,104 + NSE 290) including **278 dual-listed symbols on both
  exchanges** — counted twice in `totalMcap` and every weighted average. That,
  more than the `take: 200` truncation, is why the drill-down's market cap
  never reconciled with the ranked table: the two surfaces read different
  universes. Now filtered to NSE, matching `discover-heatmap.ts`.
- **Bounded fetch.** Removing `take: 200` to fix the truncated aggregates left
  the query unbounded — the same defect class as the unindexed sort. A
  backstop cap of 2,000 is ~5× the largest real NSE sector (Industrials ~380),
  so it never binds but the query can never run away.
- **Count source.** `count` now comes from the quoted set the aggregates are
  computed over, not the raw instrument row count.

The 11-sector peer loop (33 sequential queries) is also now 3 batched ones.
All guards mutation-tested. Post-review additions (+5 cases): the PEER
correlation query needed the same exchange filter — the first pass fixed only
the sector's own query, and this scan's original `instrumentQueryBlock()`
stopped at the first timeout label so it certified the fix while the peer
query 250 lines later still double-counted. The scan now reads both blocks and
asserts they are genuinely different text. `stale-while-error` gained an
`isPermanentError` port: a "sector has no instruments" answer must not be
masked by a 24h-old copy, which MONEY-1093 is about to make routine.

`deep-dive-fii-dii-empty-state.test.ts` (MONEY-1215) covers the two cards that
told users "FII/DII flow data not yet wired." Two defects, one string. The COPY
was our deploy state leaking onto a product surface; the QUERY behind it could
never have run — the action probed `prisma.fiiDiiFlow` through a
`prisma as unknown as { fiiDiiFlow?: … }` cast, and no `FiiDiiFlow` model has
ever existed (0 occurrences in the generated client vs 23 for
`institutionalFlow`), so the optional property was always `undefined` and the
arrays were `[]` on every request in every environment. The cast is the actual
lesson: it made unreachable code look like graceful degradation, where a real
query would have thrown and been noticed.

It cannot be "just wired up". Measured on prod 2026-08-19: `institutional_flows`
holds 8 rows whose keys are `id,date,category,segment,buyValue,sellValue,
netValue,source,createdAt,updatedAt` — no `symbol`, grain
`@@unique([date, category, segment])`, i.e. MARKET-WIDE and complete, not sparse.
`market_positioning` (92,828 rows) is participant × bucket, also no symbol.
`institutional_deals` (3,386 rows) is per-symbol but its `clientName` is free
text with no FII/DII category. `stock_shareholding` is a quarterly stake percent
and holds 12 rows for one symbol, all zeroes. So the honest outcome is the empty
state, and the suite encodes that conclusion as **schema canaries**: if
`InstitutionalFlow` ever gains `symbol`/`instrumentId`/`isin`, or
`InstitutionalDeal` gains a participant category, the tests fail and tell the
next reader the card is now buildable.

Two vacuity defences worth copying. The scans run on a comment-STRIPPED copy of
each source — the first draft did not, and failed on its own documentation,
since the comments explaining the defect necessarily quote `fiiDiiFlow` and
"not yet wired"; scanning prose would have meant the only way to keep the guards
green was to delete the explanation. And `stripComments` is itself pinned (it
must remove something, keep >40% of the file, and preserve every anchor), because
an over-eager stripper returning `""` would make every `doesNotMatch` pass.
Mutation-tested: old copy restored → 4 red; caption ungated → 1 red; phantom
probe reintroduced → 2 red; `const`→`let` → 1 red; `fiiPicks` dropped from the
payload → 1 red.

#### Navigation (`__tests__/navigation/`)

| Test File                         | Test Cases | Status |

| `url-sync-logic.test.ts`          | 31         | PASS   |
| `url-sync-seam.test.ts`           | 12         | PASS   |

MONEY-1082 — route-scoped URL writes (`lib/navigation/url-sync-logic.ts`,
consumed by `lib/hooks/useOwnedRoute.ts`). The defect: a URL write issued by a
page the user has already navigated away from re-asserts the old route and
drags them back.

Three layers, each aimed at a distinct reason the bug escaped:

- **`url-sync-logic.test.ts`** — the decisions. `decideUrlSync` /
  `decideRouteNavigation` drop off-route writes, skip no-ops, treat a trailing
  slash as the same owner and a nested route as a different one; `buildSearch`
  merge-mode preserves params owned by other components on the same route.
  `buildChatResumeHref` (MONEY-1245 follow-up) merges `chatId` into a
  `pagePath` that may already carry a query — Ask Screener scopes its history
  per mode, so the old `${pagePath}?chatId=${id}` concat emitted a second "?"
  and `URLSearchParams` folded the id into the mode value, losing BOTH. One
  case pins that broken parse directly, so the rationale survives the fix.
- **`url-sync-seam.test.ts`** — the _write_, which is what actually broke. The
  decisions were never wrong; `history.replaceState({}, …)` was. Asserts the
  live `history.state` object is forwarded by identity (it carries Next's
  `__NA` marker), that off-route and no-op writes never reach `replaceState`
  at all, and that guarded navigation forwards its options untouched.
  `useBillingCycle` shipped this bug for months _with_ a green test file
  beside it, because that file only covered `computeAnnualSavings`.
- **`no-unguarded-url-writes.test.ts`** — the static scan, mirroring
  `__tests__/ui/no-native-dialogs.test.ts` (MONEY-764). Fails on any
  `history.pushState/replaceState` that doesn't forward `window.history.state`,
  and on any `router.replace()` inside a `useEffect` outside a documented
  allowlist. `/discover/screener` had fixed this defect locally and it still
  reappeared at eight sibling sites — this scan is the propagation that fix
  lacked. Includes a liveness check (the scan can't pass vacuously) and a
  stale-allowlist check.

All four guards were mutation-tested: reintroducing `replaceState(null, …)`,
adding a raw effect-scoped `router.replace()`, swapping the forwarded state for
`{}`, and removing the off-route guard each fail the suite.

> **MONEY-1205 — why the statement mapper is a CAPTURED-fixture test.** Five
> writers each carried their own key map; three read a `period` key that does not
> exist, and the two that read `displayPeriod` correctly then read `incNpat` /
> `bsTass` / `cfOcf`, which do not exist either. Every one of those maps would
> pass a test written from the same assumption that produced it — which is
> exactly how the previous quarterly test stayed green while prod accumulated
> **zero** QUARTERLY rows: it fed the mapper the shape the broken CLIENT emitted
> rather than the shape the API emits. The inputs are now the real
> `api.tickertape.in` response bodies, verbatim under
> `packages/research/__tests__/fixtures/`.
>
> The shareholding file is the same defect one layer down and deliberately
> asserts LESS: no shareholding fixture has been captured, so it makes no claim
> about which key carries the quarter label (the mapper accepts both spellings —
> a hedge, not a finding). What it does pin is that
> `(row.prmotrHldng as number) ?? 0` is gone. `fetchShareholdingChain` runs
> Tickertape → Screener through `tryChain`, which takes the FIRST NON-NULL
> result, so a zero-filled array WON the chain, Screener never ran, and the UI
> was told "FIIs own 0.00%" — indistinguishable from a real zero.

> **MONEY-1120 (research pipeline, from the MONEY-1095 bug doc).** Three
> reported symptoms, two root causes:
>
> 1. **Alias asymmetry** — `expandSkillAliases` was applied to the post-plan
>    trim but NOT to the planner prompt, whose skill→tool table lists v2 ids
>    only. 4 of the 5 slash shortcuts (`/peer`, `/thesis`, `/earnings`,
>    `/technical`) sent a v1 alias the planner had no row for, so it planned
>    generically and the trim then cut to the alias's real tools. `/dcf` sent
>    the one real v2 id — which is why it alone returned a report.
>    `planner-skill-aliases.test.ts` pins the invariant that every preset,
>    after expansion, is planner-mappable, and keeps one case reproducing the
>    raw-alias defect so the reason expansion exists cannot be lost.
> 2. **Time-skip deadlock** — the low-time path marked tasks `failed`, but
>    `findReadyTasks` only accepts deps present in `completed`, and
>    `synthesize_report` depends on ALL tasks. Skipping one task therefore made
>    synthesis permanently unready → "Unresolvable dependency" → the bare
>    "partially completed" fallback. `releaseDependencies` frees the skipped
>    ids so synthesis runs on whatever arrived; the REGRESSION case in
>    `task-scheduling.test.ts` asserts the deadlock before and its absence
>    after.
>
> Plan sizing also moved from `8 + skills*2` to the selection's real tool count
> (floor 4, cap 28), so a single-skill shortcut stops inheriting a floor of 8.

> MONEY-798 (P3c) — `data-sources/rag-enqueue.ts` is best-effort I/O
> (`enqueueDocumentForRag` / `getRagCoverage` — prisma upsert/count, never-throw,
> DATABASE_URL-gated) and untested at that seam, same posture as the
> stock-document extract/embed I/O processors; only the PURE helpers it's built
> from are covered — `buildEnqueueKey` (idempotency identity), `computeCoverage`
> (corpus %), `initialProcessingStatus`, `isDatabaseConfigured`.

MONEY-1205/1207 added the three rows above; all three are "confident wrong
number" defects, so none of them fired an empty state.

- `stock-flags-headline` — two of the seven flag kinds publish for the WHOLE
  cash universe every session (`PRICE_BAND` 3,489 rows, `WK52_HIGH_LOW` 3,325 on
  2026-08-17), so every stock carried at least two "flags" and the strip's
  presence carried no information. The DECISION is pure and unit-tested in
  `packages/core/__tests__/market-data/stock-section-logic.test.ts`; this file
  imports those exports for the half that executes and reads the JSX source for
  the half that cannot be mounted in `node:test`, asserting STRUCTURE (which
  identifier feeds the render, which branch guards a suffix) so a copy edit does
  not red the suite.
- `fund-composition-auto-trigger` — the mount effect called
  `triggerExtraction()` whenever the cache was empty, with no gate on the ETF
  page, so one visit to any of ~446 NSE ETFs burned a Gemini call. The rule now
  lives in `shouldAutoExtractComposition` and the file tests BOTH layers: the
  real exported rule over its full input space (exactly 1 of 24 combinations may
  trigger) and that the component routes through it rather than re-implementing
  or ignoring it.
- `financials-units-and-ttm` — `StockFinancials` money columns are CRORES; the
  tab divided by 1e7 again, rendering HDFC Bank's ₹4,70,915.93 Cr revenue as
  **₹0.05 Cr**. Second defect in the same table: `parsePeriodKey("TTM")` finds no
  digits, so the freshest figure sorted LAST and was dropped entirely by
  `.slice(0, 6)` for any symbol with 7+ annual rows.

`fund-identity` is driven through the REAL exported function via its injectable
`db` port — no database and no `require.cache` mocking. The measurement behind it:
541 active ETF rows, ALL with an ISIN, 307 distinct ISINs (NSE + BSE dual
listings), and every one of the 307 joins a `mutual_fund_masters` row — while
`/etf/SBIETFQLTY` rendered AMC "Sbi", category "Other", benchmark "Other". The
row was one `select` away the whole time. `amfiSchemeCode` was populated on 0 of
them, which is why the write-through is what turns the join into a lookup.

`fund-route-canonical` asserts on source text by necessity — these are React
server components whose behaviour is `redirect()` and JSX props, neither
reachable without a Next runtime and a database — so each assertion targets the
specific line a defect lived on rather than the general shape of the file.

`fund-key-stats-states` splits three states the grid used to render as one bare
`-`: NAV history not loaded yet (a backfill is queued), the fund is younger than
the window, and history exists but is too sparse inside it to be confident.

#### FIRE Engine Package — `packages/fire/__tests__/` (MONEY-1079, new)

Most of `packages/fire` is exercised from `apps/web/__tests__/fire/*` through
the re-export shims, so this package holds only what apps/web CANNOT reach:
the server-turn save targeting, which exists solely for `apps/api`'s
`POST /v1/fire/:id/turn`.

| Source File (`packages/fire/src/`)        | Test File                      | Test Cases | Status |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------- | ------ |
| `scenarioTarget.ts` (`createScenarioOps`) | `scenario-save-target.test.ts` | 10         | PASS   |

Pins a permanent-data-loss invariant: after a turn loads a different saved
scenario, `ServerFireActions` holds THAT plan, so the save must re-point at it
— persisting to the path scenario id would overwrite it with another plan's
numbers. Driven through the real `ServerFireActions` (the
`Object.assign`-over-the-working-copy behaviour is what makes the bug
possible); verified to fail 5/10 against the pre-fix logic.

The last 5 cases build the key with the web app's REAL `generateCacheKey` and
assert the GLOSSARY patterns actually match it. Every other case here compares
strings to strings, which cannot catch a pattern that is internally tidy but
misses the key it targets. That became load-bearing when /help's glossary moved
from a 10-minute TTL to 30 days: the long TTL is only safe because a publish
purges the entry, and a missed purge shows up as /help serving a month-old
glossary with nothing in the logs. One case pins why the pattern's trailing
`:*` is required (it spans the `default` version segment), since it reads like
a typo and deleting it would silently unhook the purge.

## Running Tests

```bash
# Run all tests
yarn test

# Web app tests only
yarn workspace @usemoney/web test

# Specific test suites
yarn workspace @usemoney/web test:cache
yarn workspace @usemoney/web test:cache:redis     # Requires RUN_REDIS_TESTS=true
yarn workspace @usemoney/web test:email
yarn workspace @usemoney/web test:newsletter
yarn workspace @usemoney/web test:market
yarn workspace @usemoney/web test:pubsub

# Watch mode
yarn workspace @usemoney/web test:watch
```

## MONEY-1097 — Data Engine P2 (report registry + archive sync)

| Source File                                                            | Test File                                                         | Test Cases | Status |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------ |
| `packages/core/src/market-data/report-registry.ts`                     | `packages/core/__tests__/market-data/report-registry.test.ts`     | 48         | PASS   |
| `workers/src/processors/report-archive-sync-logic.ts`                  | `workers/__tests__/processors/report-archive-sync-logic.test.ts`  | 22         | PASS   |
| `workers/src/lib/pubsub-dedupe-logic.ts` (MONEY-1204)                  | `workers/__tests__/lib/pubsub-dedupe-logic.test.ts`               | 40         | PASS   |
| `workers/src/processors/dead-letter-consumer-logic.ts` (MONEY-1204)    | `workers/__tests__/processors/dead-letter-consumer-logic.test.ts` | 34         | PASS   |
| `workers/src/processors/alert-evaluator-logic.ts` (MONEY-1204 / 14e.3) | `workers/__tests__/processors/alert-evaluator-logic.test.ts`      | 53         | PASS   |

The registry test pins **golden URLs** rather than asserting "contains the
date", because the failure it guards is silent: a wrong token case or path
segment yields a 404, and a 404 legitimately means "market holiday / not
published yet" in this system — so a broken URL and an ordinary non-trading day
are indistinguishable in the logs _and_ in `MarketDataSyncLog`. Pinning the
whole string is the only check that fails loudly when a pattern is edited. It
also asserts the table's core invariant: **no family may be `enabled` with
`provenance: "unverified"`**.

`report-archive-sync.ts` (I/O seam) and `routes/report-archive-sync.ts`
(ACK-200-on-throw) are untested at this layer — only the pure logic the
processor calls is covered, the same posture as the investor-rollup and
stock-document-extract I/O seams.

`feed-payload.test.ts` gained 2 cases for the MONEY-1097 empty-JSON rule (a bare
`{}`/`[]` is ABSENT; a row-less-but-plausible payload is still accepted). Both
use UNPADDED fixtures: the first version padded them to 40 bytes to clear
`minBytes`, which meant the assertion never exercised the 2-byte payload its own
comment described — a shadow test. The check now runs before the `minBytes` and
`kind` dispatch, so it is reachable for every feed.

### MONEY-1168 — a failed URL import showed a bare FAILED with no reason

| Source File                                  | Test File                                               | Test Cases | Status |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------ |
| `workers/src/processors/document-failure.ts` | `workers/__tests__/processors/document-failure.test.ts` | 14         | PASS   |

A failed import rendered status FAILED, size `-`, and nothing else, so "the
remote host refused us", "the link is wrong" and "our own pipeline broke" were
indistinguishable. That is not cosmetic: it masked a real investigation. The URL
from the report (a tcs.com annual report PDF) answers **403 to every client** —
a Chrome User-Agent gets the identical refusal, and our fetcher is fine against
ordinary public PDFs — so `handleFetchUrl` throwing on `!response.ok` was
CORRECT. Because the card also carried a wrong name at the time (MONEY-1166),
an upstream 403 looked exactly like a defect in this feature.

The tests pin the two properties that are easy to regress. **Sanitisation:**
every message is built from a fixed template plus a numeric status, never from
an error's own text, so no stack trace, internal IP or GCS path can reach the
UI by construction — asserted directly against an `SsrfBlockedError` carrying a
private IP and a Prisma error naming `mongo:27017`. **Retryability:** 403 and
404 are terminal while 429, 5xx and timeouts are not, and the 403 case asserts
the copy does NOT say "try again", because inviting a retry on a permanent
refusal sends the user in a loop.

Two structural cases earn their place. One pins that `RemoteFetchError.status`
is a NUMBER — the old code threw `Error("Fetch failed: 403 Forbidden")` and
regexing that back apart is the stale-copy drift this repo keeps hitting. The
other asserts every classified message fits `MAX_FAILURE_REASON_LENGTH` without
truncation, so a template that grows past the card's one-line budget fails here
rather than silently rendering an ellipsis in production.

Untested at this layer, matching the posture of the other I/O seams:
`document-process.ts` itself (the Prisma write of `processingError`, the
PROCESSING-transition clear) and the `DocumentCard` rendering.

The natural spelling gets it WRONG and the test says why: `Number(null)` is 0, `Number("")` is 0, and BOTH pass `Number.isFinite`, so `Number.isFinite(Number(x)) ? Number(x) : null` records an absent generation as a confident `0` — a version pin matching no object that has ever existed, and a fail-open default where this repo's rule is that "couldn't determine" gets its own value. Pins that null/undefined/"" are NULL, that a real generation (~1.758e15, inside MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) survives as a number, that a GENUINE 0 is preserved because the caller decides what it means, and that garbage is null rather than NaN. ### MONEY-1101 — Data Engine P7 (BSE historical depth)

| Source File                                               | Test File                                                         | Test Cases | Status |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------ |
| `packages/core/src/market-data/bhavcopy-bse-legacy.ts`    | `packages/core/__tests__/market-data/bhavcopy-bse-legacy.test.ts` | 17         | PASS   |
| `packages/core/src/market-data/feed-payload.ts` (BSE SPA) | `packages/core/__tests__/market-data/feed-payload.test.ts`        | 22         | PASS   |

Every fixture is cut from bytes www.bseindia.com actually served on
**2026-08-13**, not invented. Two cases are marked REGRESSION and are the reason
this file exists:

1. **An unrecognised header returns `null`, never `[]`.** A failed parse and an
   empty file must be different values — MONEY-1189 lost 37 windows because they
   were the same one and the run reported `DONE … emptyChunks=0` while data was
   missing. The parse job turns that `null` into a throw, so the file stays
   **un-checkpointed** and is retried; `[]` would have checkpointed `ZERO` and
   read as a legitimately empty trading day forever after. Both halves of the
   contract are asserted — the unknown header AND the recognised-but-row-less
   file, so the guard cannot be "fixed" by making everything fail.
2. **The format drifts INSIDE a single year.** BSE's `EQ_ISINCODE_` file has
   `FILLER1` as column 16 on 2017-01-03 and `TRADING_DATE` on 2017-07-03.
   Detection is therefore by column NAME with `TRADING_DATE` optional; a parser
   calibrated on the later file returns zero rows for every early-2017 day.

The `feed-payload` cases pin the one guard standing between an 18-year backfill
and ~4,500 archived copies of BSE's homepage: BSE answers an **absent** file with
200 + its Angular SPA page (a constant 13,850 bytes), never a 404, so both
families are declared `format: "zip"` and rejected on the `PK\x03\x04` magic.

`dateFromArchiveKey` gained 4 cases for the BSE `DDMMYY` filenames
(`eq020107_csv.zip`, `EQ_ISINCODE_150323.zip`). Without that branch every object
in the backfill is skipped as "no date token" — the same failure that dropped all
4,836 gross-delivery files, at ~10x the volume. The two-digit year is resolved
against the key's own `/YYYY/MM/` segments and a disagreement returns null, so a
mis-filed object is never stamped with a guessed century.

`writeCash` skipped EVERY existing `(instrumentId, date)` cell, so wherever a
YAHOO row had landed first the authoritative exchange bhavcopy was discarded —
and the day was still checkpointed DONE, i.e. success reported, data lost. Prod
measured RELIANCE at 297 exchange rows against 7,646 Yahoo, while NIFTYBEES
(which Yahoo never covered) was complete back to 2002. The re-parse reclaimed
454,157 cells and cut OHLC violations from 53,069 to 7,860.

The load-bearing cases are `upgrades a YAHOO row instead of skipping it` (the
exact production shape — nothing asserted it before) and `is idempotent: a
second pass over its own output upgrades nothing`. The second is not ceremony:
BHAVCOPY and BHAVCOPY_HIST rank EQUAL, so if equality ever upgraded, every
routine re-parse would rewrite every row it already wrote.

`candle-integrity` covers TWO OPPOSITE repairs, which is the point of
classifying before fixing. Yahoo under-reports the RANGE (`open==high==low`
with a real close), so the range is widened to span observed prices. NSE's
1995-96 files put PREVCLOSE in the OPEN column — verified against the archived
bytes, `ACC,EQ,3338.35,3450,3341,3386.55,0.0,3338.35` — so there the open is
rebuilt from [low, high] and the range is left alone. Applying either repair to
the other class would corrupt it. Fixtures are real prod rows.

The K-miss cases carry the weight. P1 proved NSE's archive is SPARSE
(1994-11-03 present, 11-04 a genuine 404, 12-01 present), so a walker that
treats any 404 as end-of-history silently amputates everything past the first
hole **and reports success**. The tests pin that an in-range miss never ends a
range however long the run, that only K consecutive misses BELOW the declared
floor do, and that an ERROR never counts toward it — an error means we never
learned whether the file exists, so letting a throttling exchange convince the
walker that history ended is the worst possible reading of a transient failure.

`scripts/jobs/feed-backfill.ts` (the I/O job) is untested at this layer — same
posture as the other I/O seams; only the pure decisions it calls are covered.

Six wiring properties no pure test can see: the upsert is keyed on `tiingoId` so an overlapping poll re-delivering the same article writes ONCE; `written` is incremented AFTER the upsert resolves (MONEY-1255); an unknown ticker never reaches the `create` payload and IS counted; the request window is built from `lastCrawl - overlap`; the cursor advances from what LANDED, never from what was asked for; and the stored payload has no article-body column of any name. MONEY-1309 follow-up: "the cursor advances from what LANDED" was true and NOT sufficient — the feed is newest-first ACROSS DAYS and the next window is DAY-granular, so a truncated 3-day catch-up stamped day 3 and days 1-2 were never asked for again, while the run reported `ok: true` with `selected === written` and `failed: 0`. Four new properties, each asserted END TO END by running a SECOND poll and checking the orphaned day is still inside the window it asks for: the write-budget tail and an individually-refused row both bound the watermark; a walk that stopped short (offset ceiling, budget, or a 404 on page two) holds it entirely; and truncation now flips `ok`. Plus D4 — a PARTIAL master lookup omits `tickers` from the UPDATE, so a run that could not ask completely can never shrink a correct array. Mutation-verified: unconditional newest-written -> 4 red, `ok` without the truncation terms -> 5 red, `windowComplete` defaulted true -> 3 red, budget tail not recorded -> 2 red, refused row not recorded -> 2 red, always-write-tickers -> 2 red, `selected` not counting the skipped tail -> 1 red). **MONEY-1507 (C1)** adds the NEWS-event leg: every STORED article becomes one `InstrumentEvent` per RESOLVED listing, and the three cases test the JOIN rather than the halves — an article whose row was never written emits NOTHING (an event claiming a story `us_news_articles` does not hold is a notification pointing at nothing), a THROWING writer is COUNTED and the cursor decision still runs (an un-advanced watermark costs a re-poll; one advanced past an unwritten row loses it for good), and a `[control]` case asserts the PRODUCTION default is the real writer, because `run()` injects a no-op for the other 38. MONEY-1198 added the six suites above. Each pins a defect that produced a
PLAUSIBLE wrong answer rather than an error, which is why none of them was
caught by the surrounding coverage:

- `amfi-mf-provider` — `NAVAll.txt` interleaves 90 SECTION headers with 52 AMC
  headers and both are semicolon-free, so section names were stored as
  `amcName` for 16 live rows.
- `market-movers` — NSE spells the parameter `loosers`; the correct English
  `losers` returns **HTTP 200** with a 32-byte error body, which a parser reads
  as "nothing fell today". `net_price` is a PERCENT (not rupees) and can
  disagree in SIGN with `perChange` (FEDERALBNK: `perChange` −0.01 yet served in
  the GAINERS list), so direction must come from the endpoint, never a sign test.
- `xbrl-projection-write` — provenance is compared as four scalars, not a deep
  `JSON.stringify`: a Mongo round-trip does not preserve key order, so deep
  equality passes in a fake store and churns every run in prod.
- `yahoo-auth-deadline` — its own FILE because the auth cache is module-global; a
  sibling that warmed it would make the handshake a no-op and the suite would
  pass by exercising nothing.
- `discover-movers-freshness` — the movers panel ranked the PREVIOUS session and
  captioned it "today".

MONEY-1186 (Wave 2) — every one of these six suites is pinned to REAL committed
bytes, not hand-written samples, because the defects they guard are invisible in
a synthetic fixture: NSE's own participant totals are off by one contract on the
OI file, an AMC's `.xls` is actually OOXML while another's inner `.xls` is
genuinely OLE2, and the modern filing index reports `totalCount: 7091` beside
the 20 records it actually returned.

Four of the defects these caught were in code written earlier in the SAME
session, three of them contradicting their own explanatory comments — the
draining denominator in `judgeSwitchoverReadiness` was committed inside the
function whose comment cited MONEY-1196 as the reason not to. The
`xbrl-filing-index` and `xbrl-projection` suites were written by an agent whose
brief was "find defects, do not fix them; a failing test is the deliverable",
which is why they found anything at all.

MONEY-1195 — the FII/DII suite is two halves on purpose. The key assertions
prove the `FAMILY_BY_PREFIX` row exists (without it `archiveNseJsonResponse`
returns a null key, counts a `skipped`, and reports success while writing
nothing); the source-scan assertions prove the fetcher actually calls the seam
on BOTH its decode paths. Either half alone is a shadow test — MONEY-1193's
scan was green precisely because file granularity could not see that three
functions in an otherwise-compliant file bypassed the seam.

The constituent fixtures are REAL archived bytes (the Bank Nifty file that
proved the hand-pinned static list stale: 12 names pinned, 14 real). The
archive-wrapper tests pin the deliberate exclusions — per-symbol paths and
unknown endpoints never archive — because "archives everything" and "archives
what the table names" fail in opposite directions, and only the second is
recoverable by adding a row.

`nse-filings-archive` is the WIRING half of that pair, added by MONEY-1189
audit gap #6: the wrapper being correct proved nothing about three fetchers
that never called it. It stubs `globalThis.fetch` (ky resolves it at request
time) so no socket opens and `getSession` never sleeps, and uses 404 rather
than 5xx for the failure cases — ky retries 500/502/503/504 by default, which
would arm real backoff timers and orphan the run.

`scripts/jobs/fo-summary.ts` and `scripts/jobs/feed-parse.ts` (the I/O
harnesses) are untested at this layer — same posture as feed-backfill above;
their math/parsers are the covered pure modules.

Cloud Build caps ONE argument at 10,000 chars, and both specs pipe an entire
`service.yaml` through a single inline `bash -c` arg. Adding four lines of env
var looks harmless and passes build, tests and type-check — then fails at DEPLOY
time with `build step 2 arg 1 too long`. That is exactly what happened when
`FEED_ARCHIVE_MODE` was added with a verbose comment block: 9,552 → 10,829.

The fix was relocating commentary OUT of the heredoc (comments outside the arg
cost nothing); this test stops that arrangement rotting back, and warns at 700
chars of headroom rather than at the wall. It **strips the YAML block
indentation** before measuring — a raw line count overcounts by ~2,000 chars
here and would both hide real overruns and fail valid specs.

### MONEY-1194 — QA feed-replay health guard

| Source File                                      | Test File                                                   | Test Cases | Status |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------ |
| `packages/core/src/market-data/replay-health.ts` | `packages/core/__tests__/market-data/replay-health.test.ts` | 11         | PASS   |

QA ran `FEED_ARCHIVE_MODE=replay` against a working prod→QA `feeds/` mirror and
still scraped **100%** of the daily bhavcopy, every weekday, for weeks —
`replayHits=0 replayMisses=2` on 2026-08-13. Prod archived day D at 21:00 IST on
D, QA asked for day D at 21:00 IST on D, and the mirror only copied at 00:45 IST
on D+1; the archive key is date-stamped, so the request could never be
satisfied. Nothing failed, because a replay miss falls back to the exchange **by
design** and `MarketDataSyncLog.source` reads "BHAVCOPY" either way. The
counters that told the true story were already printed in the summary line and
nothing asserted on them.

The schedule fix is in `scripts/ops/setup-scheduler.sh` (a second 21:15 IST
mirror execution + QA's bhavcopy moved to 21:30, same IST calendar day). These
tests cover the other half: the pure verdict the worker now logs and meters.

The load-bearing cases are `REGRESSION: total miss is LOUD` (the measured
production shape) and `no reads is NOT a failure` — an alert that fires on a run
that asked the archive for nothing would be ignored within a week, taking the
real signal with it. `partial miss is degraded but INFO` pins the same trade-off
in the other direction: a feed the exchange never published misses on QA
forever, so it must not page. All four mutations were checked to fail the suite
(flipping the mode guard, dropping the `storeRegistered` arm, promoting
`partial-miss` to warn, silencing `total-miss`).

`workers/src/processors/bhavcopy-sync.ts` (the I/O seam that routes the verdict
to `log.warn` + `metrics.increment("feed.archive.replay.degraded")`) is untested
at this layer — same posture as every other processor I/O seam; only the pure
decision it calls is covered.

### Pre-push gate ↔ CI parity (MONEY-1164)

| Source File                   | Test File                                          | Test Cases | Status |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------ |
| `.claude/hooks/run-verify.sh` | `apps/web/__tests__/ci/verify-gate-parity.test.ts` | 10         | PASS   |

`yarn verify:push` exists to guarantee CI will be green, and `pre-push-gate.sh`
blocks pushing without its marker — so the promise holds only while the gate's
phases are a SUPERSET of the `test` job's steps in `.github/workflows/test.yml`.
Three divergences had opened up silently:

1. CI runs `yarn test:coverage-check`; the gate did not. PR #285 passed the gate
   (build 23/23, 24,478 tests, marker written) and went red on GitHub with
   "TEST-COVERAGE.md says 930 test files; 931 exist on disk". That check counts
   a SHARED file, so another branch landing tests can turn it red — exactly the
   drift a pre-push gate should catch.
2. CI sets `NODE_OPTIONS: --max-old-space-size=4096`; the gate set nothing, so
   `apps/web#build` OOM'd (SIGABRT) on a normal dev machine after ~5 minutes of
   otherwise-green work. Node sizes its default old-space from system RAM, so
   the same tree OOMs in one place and passes in another.
3. CI runs `yarn db:generate`; the gate did not. turbo's `build` task
   `dependsOn` it but `type-check` does not, and the gate type-checks FIRST — so
   it read whatever Prisma client `node_modules` held, which after a branch
   switch is the other branch's schema. Observed as
   `error TS2353: 'processingError' does not exist in type 'UserDocumentSelect'`,
   which reads like an application bug rather than a stale client.

A gate that checks LESS than CI is worse than no gate: it turns "CI is red" into
"CI is red and I was told it wouldn't be", which is how the `VERIFY_GATE_BYPASS=1`
habit starts. None of this is visible in review — both files look fine
individually, and the defect is the RELATION between them, which is what a test
can hold and a comment cannot.

The guard parses both files: every CI `run:` command must have a counterpart
phase or an explicit `NOT_MIRRORED` entry with a reason (runner bootstrap like
`corepack enable` and `yarn install`, and `yarn test:smoke`, which belongs to
the separate `smoke` job and is a strict subset of the gate's
`yarn test --force`). It also pins the heap ceilings EQUAL in both directions —
a smaller local ceiling fails work CI would accept, a larger one passes work CI
will OOM on — that `NODE_OPTIONS` is only defaulted when unset (or the
documented 8192 escape silently does nothing), that `db:generate` precedes
`type-check`, and that every failure path removes the marker rather than
leaving a stale one that would still unlock a push.

Mutation-verified against the pre-fix script: 5 of the 6 original cases fail,
and the one that passes is the sanity check that both files parsed.

A 7th case exists because the first attempt at this fix was itself a CI-parity
violation. The heap ceiling was `export`ed, which raised it for the test phase
too — but test.yml sets `NODE_OPTIONS` on the `Typecheck` step and NOT on
`Run tests`. Every `node:test` worker then grew its heap further before
collecting, and on a memory-pressured machine that produced 30s
`testTimeoutFailure`s with **zero failing test cases**: four unrelated files per
run, a different four each run, every one of them green in isolation
(`pull-subscriber` 66/66 in 3s; the `gemini` trio 163/163). The ceiling is now
applied per-phase to type-check and build only, and the case asserts it is never
exported and never reaches the test invocation.

That failure signature is worth recognising: a task-level death with `# fail 0`
is an environment problem, not a broken assertion, and the remedy is bounding
resources — never re-running until it passes.

**MONEY-1274 (2026-08-28)** — `db-first-coverage.test.ts`, 14 cases. The DB-first
short-circuit in `fetch-income-statement`, `fetch-balance-sheet` and
`fetch-cash-flow` gated on "the DB has ANNUAL rows", which is not the question
"can the DB answer what was asked". `stock_financials` holds 32,359 rows and
ZERO of `periodType: "QUARTERLY"` (measured 2026-08-28 — `XBRL_PROJECTION_APPLY`
ships `"false"` in both cloudbuild specs, so the projection has never written a
row), so a `quarterly: true` call returned on the annual rows and never reached
Yahoo's `*HistoryQuarterly` module — the only source that has them. The caller
got `success: true` with no `quarterly` key and nothing threw, so the model
reported "no quarterly data" for exactly the 2,123 covered large caps.

5 unit cases on the extracted predicate (including the post-projection case, so
the fix cannot ossify into a permanent Yahoo detour) + 9 scan cases pinning that
all three tools call it, read QUARTERLY _before_ deciding, and still return the
DB annual with an explicit `quarterlyUnavailable` marker rather than the
`success: false` that previously made asking for quarterly _lose_ the annual.

**MONEY-1274 Bug 3 (2026-08-28)** — `page-anchor.test.ts`, 15 cases.
`getSystemPrompt` resolved its page prompt with an EXACT key lookup, and every
path the app sends is a dynamic route, so all of them fell back to the generic
`BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` — verified by running the real function: `/analysis/<id>`,
`/roast/<id>`, `/stocksage`, `/stock/RELIANCE`, `/discover/screener`,
`/paper-trading/chat`. `/analysis` has had a tailored prompt the whole time and
had never once been served, because nothing sends the bare key. The dynamic
segment — the SUBJECT — was discarded too, so nothing told the model which stock
or report was on screen. Cause of MONEY-1155 #33, #34, #43 and #44.

Segment-aware longest-match resolution, plus an anchor line prepended to
whichever prompt is chosen — so the pages with no tailored prompt of their own,
which are exactly the context-blind ones, still get their subject named. Cases
cover the segment boundary (`/analysis-archive` must NOT match `/analysis`),
longest-match precedence, list pages getting NO anchor (an invented subject is
worse than none), and a [security] case proving the sanitizer is applied —
`pagePath` is request-body input being interpolated into a system prompt.

**MONEY-1274 / MONEY-1155 #30 (2026-08-31)** — `insufficient-input.test.ts`, 17
cases. "All computations are failing" was a CASCADE, not an engine fault.
`compute_growth_metrics` returned `success: false, error: "At least 2 annual
statements required"` when handed a thin input; `success: false` makes the
executor mark the task FAILED, and `buildUnavailableSourceLines` then lists it
under "FAILED / UNAVAILABLE SOURCES". So when `fetch_income_statement` returned
nothing — ~90% of symbols, and EVERY quarterly request before this ticket — the
report told the user the computation broke. The arithmetic was never reached.

`insufficientInput` returns `success: true` + `available: false` + a reason and
the SHORTFALL (`needed` / `got`), matching the shape 27 of the 63 compute tools
already used rather than inventing a third convention. NINETEEN unambiguous
data-insufficiency guards converted across 18 tools — growth-metrics, beta,
drawdown, correlation-matrix, forward-scenarios, var, risk-adjusted-returns,
technical-analysis, strategy-fit, valuation-bands (3), relative-valuation,
sector-aggregates, revenue-mix, earnings-estimates, earnings-surprise,
comparison-scores, commodity-correlation (2), cash-flow-quality.

The distinction is deliberate and pinned: a CALLER error — a required parameter
never supplied, e.g. `compute-macro-impact`'s "sector is required" — still
returns `success: false`, because that is a real defect in the run and hiding it
would be the opposite mistake. A case asserts that guard is untouched.

NINE expectations CHANGED deliberately, across `compute-drawdown.test.ts`,
`compute-var.test.ts` and `compute-risk-adjusted-returns.test.ts`: each
asserted `success: false` for thin input, i.e. each pinned the very behaviour
that made a thin input read as a failed computation. They now assert the
unavailable contract AND that no fabricated number comes back — stronger than
the boolean they replaced.

The CALLER-error half is pinned over the WHOLE tool directory rather than one
file: the conversion ran as a script over 19 guards, so the risk is not that one
was missed but that the pattern matched something it should not have. Five
caller-error messages are asserted still present as `success: false` and
asserted NOT converted.

**MONEY-1274 / MONEY-1155 #27 (2026-08-31)** — Claude models reachable on a paid
plan. `model-registry-claude.test.ts` 11 -> 17 cases. Claude was ALLOWLIST-ONLY:
all five models carry `founderOnly: true`, and the gate
(`isClaudeAvailableForEmail`) knew about emails and nothing else, so a paying
PREMIUM subscriber could not reach Claude at all.

No new concept was added. Each model already declares `requiresPlan` — the
purpose-built knob, enforced by rank in `isModelAvailableOnPlan` — and every
Claude entry declares "PRO". A restricted model is now allowed when the user's
plan satisfies the model's OWN requirement, so narrowing Claude to PREMIUM later
is a one-field edit rather than a code change. The email allowlist is KEPT as an
override: the founder keeps access on any plan, and `CLAUDE_ALLOWED_EMAILS`
remains the documented route for interns without a subscription.

The picker and the server gate now read ONE exported rule (`isClaudeEntitled`).
Widening the picker alone would have been worse than doing nothing: a PREMIUM
user would see Claude, pick it, and silently be answered by Gemini. A case
asserts the two agree across FREE / PRO / PREMIUM.

`isClaudeConfigured()` remains the floor — no key or kill-switch off means no
Claude for anyone, plan regardless; both are asserted.

NOTE how the signature change was caught. The four existing picker tests kept
PASSING at runtime after `planId` became required, because the missing argument
became `undefined` -> FREE -> Claude hidden, which happened to match the old
"non-founder sees no Claude" expectation. Only `packages/core`'s TEST type-check
(`tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) surfaced the arity error — the gate MONEY-1118
added and this branch repaired earlier.

**MONEY-1274 empty-success (2026-08-31)** — `chain-empty-success.test.ts`, 7
cases. The three statement tools ended their Screener fallback with an
UNCONDITIONAL `return { success: true, data: { annual } }`. `annual` is empty on
every real run: the chain has been Screener-only since MONEY-1220, and
`ScreenerFinancialData` carries `annualRevenue` / `annualProfit` / `annualRoe`
and has NO `income` / `balanceSheet` / `cashFlow` array — so the key it reads is
always `undefined` and maps to zero rows. The model received `success: true`
with an EMPTY statement list and read it as "this company has no statements".

It mattered more than it looks: that return sat BEFORE the DB-annual fallback
and `describeUnavailable` added earlier in this same ticket, so whenever
Screener answered it silently PREEMPTED both — the honest "not covered vs lookup
failed" message and the "report the annual we already hold" rescue were
unreachable on exactly the path they were written for. Both returns per file
(happy path + catch-block mirror) are now gated on `annual.length > 0`.

A case asserts the PREMISE rather than assuming it: if `ScreenerFinancialData`
ever gains those arrays the fallback starts producing rows again and the guard
should be revisited, so the test fails loudly instead of quietly describing a
shape that changed.

Two of these cases initially failed against CORRECT code, both my error:
`lastIndexOf` picked the catch-block return, which legitimately sits after
`describeUnavailable`; and comment-stripping ate the interface anchor the slice
depended on. Fixed to use the first return and the raw source.

The wiring scan strips comments before matching, for the same reason the
anchor-context scan does: these files now EXPLAIN the old `success: false` shape
in prose, and matching the explanation would fail a corrected file.

**MONEY-1274 / MONEY-1155 #43 (2026-09-02)** — `anchor-roast.test.ts`, 14 cases.
The previous commit gave `/roast/<id>` an ANCHOR, so the prompt said "ground
answers and follow-up suggestions in THIS roast's specific findings" — and
nothing loaded them. `assembleAnchorContext` returned early for every kind
except `research`, so the model was INSTRUCTED to cite findings it could not
see, which is worse than silence: an instruction to be specific about absent
data invites inventing it.

Deliberately NOT routed through `formatAnchoredReport`. That renderer looks for
`label|event|title|name` then `value|impact|text|summary`, while a roast carries
`{symbol, pnlPercent, roast}` and `{sector, percentage, verdict, comment}` —
neither `symbol` nor `sector` is in its list, so both would render as NOTHING.
An empty block, no error. Cases are built from the real production shape so that
stays asserted rather than assumed.

The roast shape IS stable, unlike the research report: all 14 recent rows carry
exactly ONE key-set where 35 reports carried seven. Reads are still guarded.
`roastNarrative` is deliberately omitted — several hundred words of comedy that
would crowd out the structured findings that make a suggestion specific.

Ownership cases cover BOTH id forms: `/roast/<id>` carries either a sessionId
(UUID) or a Mongo ObjectId, and the page discriminates on `includes("-")`. Two
`where` branches, both pinned to carry `userId`, plus a case asserting the
page's own discriminator has not drifted from the loader's.

**MONEY-1274 single-owner prompts (2026-09-08)** —
`packages/core/__tests__/gemini-prompts-single-owner.test.ts`, 5 cases. THE
BIGGEST FINDING OF THIS TICKET, and it was found by a user question about model
switching rather than by any test.

The page-anchor fix for #33/#34/#44 was written into
`apps/web/lib/gemini/prompts.ts` — a FORK with ZERO production importers. The
live implementation is `packages/core/src/gemini/prompts.ts`, reached via
`@usemoney/core` from `conversation.ts`. So the fix compiled, its tests passed
against the fork, and the anchor never reached a model. `/analysis` still fell
back to the generic prompt; the model still could not name the stock on screen.

Third duplicate-copy failure in this branch: (1) compute guards tested from two
workspaces, (2) main's `internalOnly` tests against a changed signature, (3)
this. Unit tests CANNOT catch it — a test importing the fork proves the fork
works — so the new guard checks the module GRAPH: exactly one definition of
`getSystemPrompt` and of each anchor helper, the deleted fork has not returned,
the live copy resolves by segment rather than exact key, and the anchor is
sanitized. Verified by positive control: recreating the fork makes it fail.

The merge was NOT a clean supersede, and assuming it would have been was the
near-miss. Comparing EXPORT NAMES said core was a strict superset; comparing
BEHAVIOUR said otherwise, in both directions:

- the fork's `formatFireContext` was richer (Cr/L money, asset allocation,
  expense breakdowns, sanitized names) — ported here, then REVERTED, because
  this copy has behaviours the fork lacked ("50K" formatting, 0-defaults) that
  its own tests pin. Neither is a superset. Swapping it changes what the FIRE
  chat emits in production today, which is a product decision and not this
  ticket's job. Recorded rather than done; the fork's version is in git.
- the fork's `formatHoldingsContext` used `any[]` (CLAUDE.md forbids it) and
  divided by `totalInvested` with NO zero guard. Core's has both fixed, so
  core's is kept.
- the two `/analysis` prompt texts differ (the fork's mentions "Quality
  Score"). Core's is what production has always served; left alone.

`apps/web/__tests__/gemini/prompts.test.ts` (55 cases) is DELETED: it asserted
the fork's behaviour, and the fork is gone. `__tests__/core/gemini/prompts.test.ts`
(71 cases) already exercises the real exports and is the better file.

Proven end-to-end after the port: `/stock/RELIANCE` now yields an anchor naming
RELIANCE, and `/analysis/<id>` resolves to its tailored prompt for the first
time.

**MONEY-1274 history block replay (2026-09-07)** — `history-blocks.test.ts`,
16 cases, closes the real half of MONEY-1155 #44. Found by asking whether
context survives a mid-chat model switch; the answer turned out to be wider than
the question.

A chat message carries TWO channels — `content` (a string) and `blocks` (what
the UI renders) — and history replay sent only the first:

    parts: [{ text: msg.content }]

while every rich turn writes a STUB into `content`: "Here are the research
results:" (ChatContext.tsx:983), "Full research report loaded:" (:1150), or ""
while streaming (:2240). So a follow-up reached the model as
`assistant: "Here are the research results:"` and nothing else, and answered
from the question alone.

NOT a model-switch bug, which is what makes the framing matter: history is keyed
by chatId + userId and never by model, so a Gemini -> Claude switch loses
nothing that was present — the report was absent for BOTH. Switching just makes
it noticeable. The fix flattens blocks to TEXT at the replay boundary, which is
what every provider's client receives, so it is provider-agnostic by
construction rather than by a per-provider branch.

Chosen over the narrow alternative (load the research report from the DB when
the page anchor says `research`): that helps ONE block type on ONE page, and
there are 26 types with the same hole. Targeted renderers cover the types
carrying real substance; everything else falls through to a scalar walk, so a
type added later degrades to "some readable keys" rather than to silence.

Beyond the point cases: a message with no blocks replays BYTE-IDENTICALLY (most
turns have none, and this must not alter every conversation); truncation SAYS
how many rows it withheld, because a silently-cut list reads as the whole
answer; budgets are per message because history replays on every turn, and an
unbounded flatten would make `trimHistoryToTokenBudget` evict the OLDEST turns
to pay for the newest; every rendered field goes through the sanitizer, asserted
by planting a marker in each renderer's own fields rather than counting calls;
and two wiring assertions — that `convertToGeminiFormat` no longer replays
`msg.content` alone, and that the history cache key never gains a model, since
that is what would make a switch lose history.

**MONEY-1274 review fixes (2026-09-07)** — ten findings from the xhigh review
applied. Three mattered:

1. ELEVEN compute guards merged a CALLER error (argument absent or wrong type)
   into the same `insufficientInput` return as thin data, so a malformed tool
   call was reported to the model as "not enough data" — it would accept that as
   fact or retry the same broken call. Each is now split: absent/wrong-type
   fails the task, too-short reports unavailable. THREE were left merged on
   purpose (`compute-valuation-bands` x2, `compute-cash-flow-quality`): those
   ask "at least one of two OPTIONAL inputs", which is genuinely a data
   question, and they are listed by name in the detector rather than
   pattern-excluded so adding one is deliberate.
2. `renderBreakdown` sanitized the object KEY and interpolated the VALUE raw.
   `str()` accepts any non-empty string and `scoreBreakdown` is model-generated
   then stored, so untrusted text reached a trusted prompt section. Now
   sanitized and capped like every sibling renderer.
3. `isNonEmpty({available:false, reason})` returned TRUE — `available:false` is
   a boolean and the scalar branch accepts any boolean — so a tool that produced
   nothing rendered as a DONE task claiming it had data, defeating the
   empty-but-green guard MONEY-778 added.

The two tests that were supposed to catch (1) and (2) could not, and both are
replaced rather than patched:

- the caller-error test matched a hardcoded allowlist of message STRINGS, so
  a guard that folded a caller error into a data-shaped message passed. It now
  detects the SHAPE — any `insufficientInput` whose enclosing `if` also tests
  presence or type — with the window scoped to the immediately enclosing
  guard, because a fixed lookback spans the (correct) caller-error branch above
  it and reports a fixed file as an offender.
- the `[security]` case asserted `calls.length > 0`, which the first renderer
  satisfies before the others run. It now plants a marker in EVERY rendered
  field, including the breakdown value, and asserts none survives.

Both were verified by positive control: re-merging one guard, and restoring the
unsanitized interpolation, each made the new test fail.

Also: `getAvailableModelsForUser` gained the `internalOnly` filter its sibling
already had (the registry test titled "hides a model from EVERY caller" only
exercised the picker, and now exercises both); the quarterly DB read in all
three statement tools is gated on the annual half having passed, since the gate
fails on empty annual regardless and the result was discarded; a duplicated
identical `if (annual.length > 0)` was collapsed in all three; the roast id
dash-heuristic became an OR over both columns, with the `id` arm gated on
24-hex validity because Prisma throws for the WHOLE query on a non-ObjectId
value; and the doubled error swallow around `assembleAnchorContext` is now one
catch that logs.

**MONEY-1274 chat message flow (2026-09-07)** — `chat-message-list-flow.test.ts`,
7 cases, closes MONEY-1155 #31 ("UI needs to be fixed"). The screenshot was the
StockSage panel on an analysis page holding ONE exchange, pinned to the bottom
under ~60% blank space. `ChatMessageList` wrapped its messages in `min-h-full
flex flex-col justify-end`: the column was forced to the scroller's full height
and its children pushed to the bottom of it.

The bottom-pinning was redundant. An effect already sets `scrollTop =
scrollHeight` on `[messages, isLoading]` behind a near-bottom guard, so it
covers the OVERFLOW case; the CSS only changed anything when there was too
little content for that to matter — exactly where it looked broken.

Assertions are structural (the classes ARE the behaviour, and this runner has no
DOM to measure with), and include the guards that make the deletion safe rather
than just the deletion: the scroller keeps `h-full overflow-y-auto`, the scroll
effect and its dependency array survive, the near-bottom guard survives, and the
EMPTY state keeps its deliberate `items-center justify-center`. Visual
confirmation is still owed and is flagged on the PR.

**MONEY-1274 mode badge (2026-09-05)** — `research-mode-badge.test.ts`, 9
cases, closes MONEY-1155 #28 ("starting an advanced research still shows deep -
comprehensive"). `block.mode` is CLIENT-ONLY: it is threaded from the confirm
action's `params.mode`, and `ResearchSession` persists `skill` with no
mode/depth column, so a block rebuilt from the DB after a reload has no mode.
The old code answered that unknown with `deep: true` + `"Comprehensive"`,
fabricating BOTH halves — an advanced run reloaded as "DEEP · Comprehensive"
(the report) and a fast run as "DEEP", contradicting itself. `modeBadge()` now
returns undefined for an unknown mode and the pill renders only the halves it
has. Persisting mode would need a schema column and is out of scope; showing
less is the honest move, same correction as the failed-stage stepper above.

Beyond the point cases: `deep` and `depth` must be BOTH known or BOTH unknown
(a half-known badge is a new way to render a confident half-truth), and the
scans strip comments first because all three files now explain the old default
in prose.

**MONEY-1274 failed-stage (2026-09-03)** — `research-failed-stage.test.ts`, 7
cases. A QA deep-research run showed "RESEARCH FAILED" with the stepper
highlighting SYNTHESIZING, the last stage before COMPLETED. The DB said
otherwise: PLANNING, progress 0, steps 0, tokens 0, plan NULL, scratchpad empty,
and `updatedAt == createdAt` — the row was written once and never touched, so no
worker ever picked the job up. The CAUSE of that stall is unexplained — an
earlier version of this entry blamed a 404 at the QA push endpoint, read off an
unauthenticated `/health` GET that returns the same 404 for PRODUCTION while
production serves normally. Measured 2026-09-05: undelivered backlog ZERO on
`stock-research-qa-push`, and a run completed normally 2026-09-03. The UI defect
is ours regardless, and is what these cases pin:

    const curIdx = RUN_STAGE_ORDER.indexOf(isFailed ? "SYNTHESIZING" : stage);

EVERY failure was drawn as "four of five stages done" whatever actually
happened, so a dead queue looked like a late-stage model hiccup. That is a large
part of why this went unnoticed from 2026-08-21 (last successful run
2026-08-08). The failed stage is now derived from progress via
`stageForProgress`, which lives in `research-run.tsx` because that module owns
`RunStage` / `RUN_STAGE_ORDER` — importing the other way would be a cycle.

Beyond the point cases: every progress 0-100 must map to a stage the stepper can
place (an unknown value yields `indexOf` -1, which lights up NO node and reads
as "nothing happened" — a different wrong answer, not a fix), and the mapping
must be monotonic.

NOT fixed here, deliberately: the client's poll timeout calls
`updateActionBlock(... status: "failed")`, which is CLIENT state only — the
`ResearchSession` row is never updated, which is why three sessions still read
PLANNING. Marking them FAILED from the client would be wrong: a slow job that
later succeeds would be destroyed. The correct fix is a server-side sweeper for
jobs untouched past a deadline, which is new behaviour that cannot be verified
from here.

**MONEY-1274 Bug 2 (2026-08-29)** — `unavailable-reason.test.ts`, 13 cases. A
statement tool that found nothing returned `No income statement data found for
${symbol}`, and `buildUnavailableSourceLines` puts that string in front of the
model verbatim — so the model reported it as a finding about the COMPANY. The
same string was produced whether every source threw, our egress was blocked, or
the symbol is a genuinely uncovered SME; only the last is true.
`tryChainDetailed` (MONEY-1146) already computed the difference and had NO
caller outside its own module, so the diagnosis was calculated and discarded on
every request.

`describeUnavailable` consumes the ending: a failed lookup says it is a source
problem and tells the model not to convert it into a finding (+ sets
`metadata.sourceError`, which the RC4 synthesizer path keys off); a no-coverage
ending attributes the gap to OUR SOURCES and names the legitimate reasons
(BSE-only, SME/Emerge, recent IPO) — and deliberately does NOT set
`sourceError`, which would invent an outage, the opposite lie. A mixed ending
counts as FAILED: one throw voids the absence, because the source that failed
might have been the one holding the data.

`tickertape-off-request-path.test.ts` was WIDENED, not relaxed, in the same
change: it sliced `fetchFinancialsChain` to prove Tickertape is off the request
path, and that function now delegates, so the old slice would have scanned a
one-line stub and passed regardless. It now asserts across both halves of the
path.

**MONEY-1274 / MONEY-1155 #32 (2026-08-29)** — `anchor-report.test.ts` (8) +
`anchor-context-ownership.test.ts` (6). Naming the report was not enough: the
model still re-analysed the company instead of answering from the report on
screen. `assembleAnchorContext` loads it and `formatAnchoredReport` renders a
capped block, fed through the existing `sanitizeMemoryContext` trust boundary
as a SIBLING of the investor-memory block — merged, the cap inside that
sanitizer would let a long report silently crowd the profile out.

The renderer is defensive because the shape is not stable: 35 recent production
reports carry SEVEN distinct key-sets, and item types differ within them
(`strengths`/`risks` are strings, `catalysts` is `{event,timeline,impact}`,
`keyMetrics` is `{label,value,verdict}`). Cases are built from the real shapes;
an unrecognised object is dropped rather than JSON-dumped at the model, and an
unfinished report says it is unfinished rather than being read as findings.

The ownership cases are the important half. `pagePath` is REQUEST-BODY input, so
an unscoped read is an IDOR whose payload lands in the model's context and
therefore in the reply text. Both session tables (`/analysis/<id>` serves two,
split by id prefix) are pinned to carry `userId` in the WHERE, `findUnique` is
banned because it cannot express the compound filter, and the prefix list is
pinned against `session-routing.ts` so the two cannot drift.

NOTE the scan strips comments before matching: the source's own doc comment
NAMES the unsafe `findUnique` shape it avoids, so a raw scan matched the
explanation and failed a file that was already correct. A scan test must assert
over syntax — matching prose makes documenting a hazard indistinguishable from
committing it.

`__tests__/gemini/prompts.test.ts` — one expectation CHANGED deliberately:
`hasCustomPrompt("/fire/")` asserted `false` under "Exact key match required",
pinning the exact-key lookup that was the defect. A trailing slash must not
change a page's identity, so it now asserts `true`, with `/fireplace` still
`false` alongside it to keep the segment boundary enforced.

`tryChain` returned `null` for two endings that need opposite responses: every
source answering cleanly with no data (BSE-only, SME/Emerge, newly listed — an
ordinary answer) and every source THROWING (blocked, rate-limited, vendor layout
changed — the feature is broken). Every client returns `null` for an empty
response as well as a failure, and `tryChain` caught every exception, so the
Ownership tab rendered one empty panel for both with no log line separating
them. It could have been dead for months without a signal.

This is the half MONEY-1146 called its priority — "right now we cannot even tell
whether the feature is broken" — and the half the earlier pass explicitly
recorded as NOT achieved, in both the action and its test, because it looked
like it required changing `tryChain` for all ten consumers. It does not: a
second entry point (`tryChainDetailed` / `fetchShareholdingChainDetailed`)
carries the diagnosis while `tryChain` stays a thin wrapper, so the other nine
call sites are untouched.

The two test files are deliberately different in kind. The action test parses
source to pin the WIRING — that the error branch runs BEFORE `?? []`, since
after that collapse the two endings are already indistinguishable. The research
test EXECUTES `tryChainDetailed` against fake sources to pin the CLASSIFICATION
itself, including that a fallback chain whose first source throws and second
succeeds still reports success while carrying the error, and that it stops at
the first success (these are rate-limited third parties, not a fan-out).

Still open on MONEY-1146, and deliberately not claimed: the fetch is still on
the request path for `apps/api` (`packages/services/src/stock-tabs.service.ts`
has the failure fix but not the DB-first read), and nothing schedules a
background refresh.

### Atlas query operators ↔ index mappings (MONEY-1141 / MONEY-1128)

| Source File                             | Test File                                                  | Test Cases | Status |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------ |
| `apps/web/lib/market/content-search.ts` | `apps/web/__tests__/market/atlas-filter-operators.test.ts` | 7          | PASS   |
| `apps/web/lib/market/atlas-search.ts`   | (same)                                                     | —          | PASS   |

`content-search.ts` filtered `content_search` with the `text` operator on
`contentType`, `contentPlatform` and `status` — all mapped `token`. A `text`
operator against a token-mapped field matches NOTHING, and all three sat in
`compound.filter`, so **every Atlas content search returned zero rows in
production**. It surfaced as "no results" rather than an error because
`actions/content.ts` treats an empty Atlas result as a legitimate answer and
falls through to the service path: content search ran on the non-Atlas path in
prod with no log, no error and no metric.

The code fix (`equals` instead of `text`) landed with MONEY-1130. This test is
the part the ticket flagged as still missing — the class guard. It was the
SECOND occurrence: MONEY-1128 found the same mistake on the instrument
`exchange` filter, which survived only because no caller passed `exchange`. Two
instances of one mistake, neither caught by a test, a type, or a log, because
the index mappings live in a markdown doc that nothing connects to the query
code.

The test reads the documented mappings from `docs/setup/atlas-search-setup.md`
and fails if a token-mapped field is queried with `text`. Dual-mapped fields
(`string + token`, e.g. `category`) are deliberately excluded — `text` is
legitimate there, and flagging them would make the guard reject correct code.

Two of the six cases assert the DETECTOR, not the sources: one feeds it the
original broken query and requires both fields flagged, one feeds it legitimate
`text` queries on analysed fields and requires none. Without those, a parser
that silently matched nothing would show up as a green suite — "no violations"
and "found nothing at all" are indistinguishable otherwise.

It also strips comments before scanning, line-comments FIRST. That is not
incidental: `atlas-search.ts` explains the MONEY-1128 fix by quoting the broken
code, and the guard's first run failed on that comment while the real query
below it was already correct. The ordering matters for the reason MONEY-1143
documents — stripping blocks first lets a `//` containing `/*` swallow the code
under assertion.
